title: Roger Federer holds back tears while thanking his wife at Tennis Hall of Fame induction
description: Roger Federer got emotional honoring wife Mirka during his Tennis Hall of Fame induction in Newport. See what brought the tennis legend to tears.
fullText:
Roger Federer has never been shy about showing emotion on the tennis court, but this week it was gratitude, not victory, that brought him to tears. The Swiss legend was formally inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island, and the moment he turned to talk about his wife, Mirka, he could barely get the words out.

Federer, 45, entered the Hall as the sole player in this year's class, sharing the stage with broadcaster and journalist Mary Carillo, who was inducted in the contributor category. It capped a run that redefined men's tennis: the first man to reach 20 Grand Slam singles titles, 103 tour-level trophies, and 237 consecutive weeks at world No. 1 between 2004 and 2008. But on this particular evening in Newport, none of that seemed to be what was on his mind.

It was Mirka who opened the night, taking the stage first to introduce her husband. She reached back to where it all began — the 2000 Sydney Olympics — recalling how Andy Roddick, in the audience, once joked after losing a Cincinnati final that he couldn't believe he'd lost to a guy whose girlfriend warmed him up before matches. She closed her remarks by calling herself proud not just of the champion, but of the man behind him.

Roger Federer reveals what retirement really looks like — Food, travel, and dog kisses

Roger Federer at 45: Inside the champion's life beyond tennis

What Roger Federer had to say about sitting in the Royal Box with the Princess of Wales

Federer wasn't ready for how good she'd be at it. "She's a good public speaker. I didn't know that. A tough act to follow," he said as he took the microphone, according to Tennis Majors.

From there, the speech unraveled into one emotional pause after another — for his childhood hero Stefan Edberg, for his longtime coach Severin Luthi, and finally, for Mirka. Federer joked that he needed "tissues and sunglasses, everything to protect me right now," as reported by ESPN, before composing himself to share what's meant to him: a coach in the early days, a hitting partner before matches, a stylist when he needed one, and the person who taught him "to get more focused about tennis, and take joy in everything else."

The line that landed hardest, though, came when he talked about the life they've built together — Mirka as mother to their four children, and partner in everything since. "She and I grab each other's hands, and we run through walls," Federer said.

There was a lighter moment tucked into the tears, too. Federer gave a shoutout to Martina Navratilova, who had joined him for an exhibition doubles match the night before the ceremony. As he told the crowd, in comments reported by Yahoo Sports/Pro Football Network, "Now we're going into the Mirka bit. This is such a mess" — right before crediting Navratilova with an unlikely assist in his own love story: she was the one who first inspired Mirka to pick up a racket, which is how the two of them ended up on the same Olympic team, and eventually, as partners.

Federer closed the night the way he's closed matches for two decades — thanking the people who rarely get thanked, this time the ball kids who stood through his matches for hours on end. He made it clear that he saw them and that he used to be one of them.

title: Ohio State football makes cut for 4-star cornerback from California
description: The No. 1-rated cornerback in the state of California has trimmed his list to 12, and Ohio State is firmly in the mix.
fullText:
The Ohio State football team will finally open its 2026 season this week. Even though the Buckeyes are firmly focused on the task at hand, recruiting never stops. While the 2027 class is almost wrapped up, it's time to begin locking in commitments for 2028. As high school football has already kicked off, a four-star cornerback has put OSU in his top 12.

Ca'ron Williams is the No. 1-rated corner in the talent-rich state of California according to 247Sports composite rankings and a top 200 player overall. The Santa Margarita Catholic product is keeping the Buckeyes in the mix along with Cal, LSU, Miami, Notre Dame, Oklahoma, Oregon, Texas, Texas A&M, UCLA, USC, and Washington.

His high school team is coached by former Heisman winner and NFL quarterback Carson Palmer. The team is now 2-0 after Friday's game thanks to a pick-six from Williams, as well as a blocked extra point.

NEWS: Four-Star CB Ca’ron Williams is down to 12 Schools, a source tells @Rivals

He’s ranked as the No. 1 CB in California in the 2028 Rivals Industry Rankingshttps://t.co/uQZ2LtpiFy pic.twitter.com/57FSA7UY6B

Williams earned a scholarship offer this past April during a visit to Columbus, which left the coaching staff impressed. There's a long way to go in his recruitment, but making the cut from a long list of suitors is a step in the right direction.

title: Auburn football releases depth chart for Week 1's game vs Baylor
description: Some big questions answered on Monday when Auburn football unveiled its first depth chart of the 2026 season.
fullText:
The official depth chart for Auburn football has been released ahead of the Baylor game in Week 1 in Atlanta, Georgia, for the Aflac Kickoff game.

It is finally game week on the Plains, as head coach Alex Golesh prepares for his first game as the head coach of the Auburn Tigers. The team will head to Atlanta for Saturday's matchup against Baylor in the Aflac Kickoff Game. Some big offseason questions have been answered after the release of the depth chart.

To touch on the one many had been wondering throughout the Summer and into Fall camp is the running back room. Obviously Jeremiah Cobb is RB1, but the RB2 is where things get interesting. Omar Mabson and Bryson Washington will seem to be splitting carries at the second running back spot. At the end of the day, Auburn is just loaded at the running back position.

The one room that draws concerns is the offensive line. Jo Simmons will be starting at left tackle, Stanton Ramil at right tackle, and Cole Best at center are the clear starters on the line. When it comes to the guards, there are a ton of question marks. It will be a potential rotation of guys as they try to solidify those right and left guard roles.

title: Former NBA champion assistant Patrick Mutombo joins Kevin Young’s BYU staff
description: BYU has added a rather accomplished assistant coach to its men’s basketball staff.  Kevin Young has hired Patrick Mutombo as a new assistant for the Cougars, the program announced Monday.  Mutombo is replacing Will Voigt, who left for Boise State earlier this offseason after two years with Young in Provo.
fullText:
BYU has added a rather accomplished assistant coach to its men's basketball staff.

Kevin Young has hired Patrick Mutombo as a new assistant for the Cougars, the program announced Monday.

Welcome Home Coach 🤙 pic.twitter.com/eJznn22avd

Mutombo is replacing Will Voigt, who left for Boise State earlier this offseason after two years with Young in Provo.

"We are absolutely thrilled to welcome Patrick and his family to Provo," Young said in a statement.

"Patrick is one of the best humans I've met in the game of basketball. Cougar Nation will love him and his family. He has tremendous experience in the NBA and with USA Basketball that will be of great benefit to all of our players and staff. We couldn't be more excited to add the Mutombo family to BYU basketball."

Mutombo arrives at BYU with 10 years of experience as an NBA assistant for the Denver Nuggets, Toronto Raptors, Phoenix Suns, Milwaukee Bucks and Memphis Grizzlies, reaching the playoffs nine times in total. He won a championship with the Raptors in 2019 and spent the 2022-23 campaign alongside Young in Phoenix.

Among the notable players Mutombo helped coach are Kawhi Leonard, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kevin Durant and other All-Star talents.

In addition to his NBA résumé, Mutombo served as head coach for the Raptors' G League affiliate for two seasons and was an assistant for both the Austin Spurs and his alma mater Metro State for a year each.

As a player, he captured two Division-II national championships with Metro State and played professionally overseas from 2003-09.

Mutombo will now be part of his first Division-I coaching staff at BYU, sharing the bench with fellow assistants Tim Fanning, John Linehan, Brandon Dunson and Chris Burgess.

title: Ole Miss vs. Louisville: Here’s our cocktail of the week
description: A little something to dull the senses
fullText:
Some of you may not choose to imbibe the day of an Ole Miss game for health reasons or so you can savor every moment of football come hell or high water.

But then there is every other degenerate who frequents this blog the last 15+ years.

Before we delve into our cocktail of the week, to kickoff this series we revisit the famed "Whiskey Speech" by Noah "Soggy" Sweat, a one time Mississippi state representative, who spoke on the issue of alcohol prohibition in the 1950's.

"My friends, I had not intended to discuss this controversial subject at this particular time. However, I want you to know that I do not shun controversy. On the contrary, I will take a stand on any issue at any time, regardless of how fraught with controversy it might be. You have asked me how I feel about whiskey. All right, this is how I feel about whiskey:

If when you say whiskey you mean the devil's brew, the poison scourge, the bloody monster, that defiles innocence, dethrones reason, destroys the home, creates misery and poverty, yea, literally takes the bread from the mouths of little children; if you mean the evil drink that topples the Christian man and woman from the pinnacle of righteous, gracious living into the bottomless pit of degradation, and despair, and shame and helplessness, and hopelessness, then certainly I am against it.

But, if when you say whiskey you mean the oil of conversation, the philosophic wine, the ale that is consumed when good fellows get together, that puts a song in their hearts and laughter on their lips, and the warm glow of contentment in their eyes; if you mean Christmas cheer; if you mean the stimulating drink that puts the spring in the old gentleman's step on a frosty, crispy morning; if you mean the drink which enables a man to magnify his joy, and his happiness, and to forget, if only for a little while, life's great tragedies, and heartaches, and sorrows; if you mean that drink, the sale of which pours into our treasuries untold millions of dollars, which are used to provide tender care for our little crippled children, our blind, our deaf, our dumb, our pitiful aged and infirm; to build highways and hospitals and schools, then certainly I am for it.

This is my stand. I will not retreat from it. I will not compromise."

It doesn't get much better than that in the world of speeches given.

Also, we've got a ballgame against Louisville this week which sits in the epicenter of bourbon, so the "Whiskey Speech" seemed appropriate for this series. With that in mind, our cocktail of the week is damn simple and damn good.

COCKTAIL OF THE WEEK – LOUISVILLE

Pour bourbon into short glass and add crushed or cubed ice to your liking and enjoy

What will you be sipping on come gametime on Sunday evening? Share in the comments below. Cheers!

fullText:
Aston Villa entertained Arsenal at Villa Park earlier tonight as they hoped to secure a win at home in the Premier League. The Villans made a decent start to the game and managed to get to the half-time break with a 0-0 scoreline.

Bukayo Saka broke the deadlock for the visitors in the 59th minute. Unai Emery's men failed to mount a comeback and crashed to a lackluster 1-0 loss in front of their home fans.

Let's take a look at how each Aston Villa player fared during the clash against the Gunners.

He made one great save at the back but couldn't do much about Saka's effort.

Cash came back to defend when he could, but offered very little going forward.

He put his foot through the ball when needed, but failed to keep a clean sheet.

Torres performed his defensive duties well but lacked quality on the ball.

BIRMINGHAM, ENGLAND – AUGUST 31: John McGinn of Aston Villa argues with referee Jarred Gillett after a penalty is awarded to Arsenal which was later overturned after a VAR check during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Aston Villa FC and Arsenal FC at Villa Park on August 31, 2026 in Birmingham, England. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Maatsen had a few nervy moments at the back but was adventurous on the ball.

He anchored the midfield well but failed to make a difference going forward.

Hemmings struggled to get a foothold in the game and put in a disjointed performance at the centre of the park.

He worked his socks off, but struggled to be a threat in the final third.

Barkley got stuck in with some solid tackles and engineered two key chances on the offensive end of the field.

He managed to shine at times, but there was no goal for him tonight.

Jackson made a few decent runs with the ball but never looked like he would score.

He failed to influence the game after coming off the bench.

Abraham failed to threaten the Arsenal goal.

title: WNBA photo essay: How a record-breaking Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream dethroned the Minnesota Lynx in DeWanna Bonner’s debut
description: Swish Appeal photographer Christina Merrion captured the Dream’s big win over the Lynx.
fullText:
There's a truism in basketball that the first home game after a long road trip feels like another road game.

The Atlanta Dream proved the validity of that idea on Friday night, with a flat performance resulting in a nearly 20-point loss to the Portland Fire.

On Sunday afternoon, re-acclimated and agitated, the real Dream returned. Or, maybe the realest Dream.

For the second-straight season, the Dream secured the season series win over the Minnesota Lynx, preventing the league leaders from clinching the No. 1 seed in the WNBA playoffs with an 89-81 win. The Atlanta victory also handed Minnesota a second-straight loss for only the second time this season.

The urgency that was absent on Friday appeared with a fury on Sunday as the Dream effectively disrupted the Lynx offense on one end, evidenced by holding Rookie of the Year frontrunner and MVP candidate Olivia Miles to zero assists for only the second time this season, before executing with alacrity on the other.

Smesko said the Dream brought a "different pace", "different energy" from the beginning of the game. Smesko on the main focus coming into the game to secure the win:
Question: @EGlazeOTV 

"We thought we just had to come out with a different mindset. Like, we needed to get on the… https://t.co/76q1Kl9Y3s

Allisha Gray kickstarted things for Atlanta, both attacking the basket and draining 3s as she scored 18 of her game-high 23 points in the first half. In second half, Rhyne Howard came alive, not just scoring all of her 16 points but also seeming to score them all at just the right moments, with her triples and tough takes neutralizing any threat Minnesota tried to muster. Jordin Canada effectively picked her spots to punish the Lynx with lightning-quick drives, finishing with 16 points in addition to dishing 10 dimes. Naz Hillmon's stat line may have been a modest seven points and three rebounds, but the Dream outscored the Lynx by a game-high 21 points in her minutes, testifying to her winning impact.

And then there was Angel Reese, relentless as ever as she secured her 29th double-double of the season. Her 15 points and 11 rebounds established a new WNBA single-season record.

SHE IS THE ONE 👑

With her 29th double-double, Angel Reese now stands alone with the most in a single season in league history! WHAT A RUN! pic.twitter.com/iCinwhgYgi

The previous mark belong the partner (Alyssa Thomas) of her newest teammate, as DeWanna Bonner made her Dream debut, taking the court to standing ovation before scoring seven points, including a 3-pointer assisted by Reese, in her 17 minutes.

It was the kind of performance that made it conceivable that DeWanna could, in fact, achieve her final championship Dream in Atlanta.

Fortunately, Christina Merrion, Swish Appeal's contributing photographer, opted to attend Sunday's game, not Friday's. Here's are the scenes she captured from before, during and after what might have been Atlanta's best win of the season.

title: Texas A&M coach Mike Elko ready to stop talking start watching his Aggies play football
description: Texas A&M will open the season at home against Missouri State. That's a relief for Mike Elko, who's tired of preseason chatter.
fullText:
COLLEGE STATION - Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko believes his team is good enough to compete. He knows the Aggies have to the talent to win football games.

But ahead of Saturday's 6 p.m. season opener at Kyle Field against Missouri State, Elko reiterated that the 2026 Texas A&M team has proven nothing yet on the field.

"Finally, we get to stop talking," Elko said during his Monday news conference. "Finally, we get to stop talking about what things can be, what things can be about and we get to run out of the tunnel and go play somebody else. It's beyond past the time to go do that."

Expectations are high for the Aggies in Elko's third season with a preseason ranking of No. 8 and coming off their best season in more than a decade. Last year's team, despite losing its last two games to Texas and then Miami in the College Football Playoff, won 11 games for only the third time in three decades.

ALSO: Mike Elko's challenge? To keep Aggies among college football's best.

Plus key contributors return on both sides of the ball, including quarterback Marcel Reed and wide receiver Mario Craver, along with key transfers such as defensive end Anto Saka and left tackle Tyree Adams.

The first test comes in the form of the Bears, who made the jump from FCS to FBS last season and won seven games. Head coach Ryan Beard left before their bowl game to take the Coastal Carolina job and was replaced by former SMU offensive coordinator Casey Woods.

Elko highlighted Woods as a hot name in the offensive coordinator world in recent years. With a new staff and various new players coming in, Elko said the staff has watched film of multiple different teams to try and get a feel what Missouri State's offense might look like.

But the focus for Texas A&M will be on themselves, not their opponent come Saturday.

"We've elevated ourselves to be a team that has made the playoff, has competed to go to the SEC championship, has finished in the top 10," Elko said. "Whether this team can do that, I don't know. We'll find out when we start playing people for real"

Illinois transfer David Olano has won the starting kicker role over freshman Asher Murray.

Olano started the past two seasons for the Fighting Illini before coming to College Station in the transfer portal. He is 37 of 43 for his career with a long of 50 yards.

Elko said that Olano didn't kick much during the spring due to an injury, opening up an opportunity for Murray, an early enrollee out of Shreveport, La.

In the end, the Aggies went with the more experienced player.

"They went back and forth, and it was very, very close and very, very tight and tight because both guys were phenomenal," Elko said. "I think we have a really, really strong kicking situation."

Elko anticipates starting linebacker Daymion Sanford will play Saturday. "Probably still a little bit of a gametime decision," Elko said.

Following Sunday's NFL cut day, Elko said 32 Texas A&M players made NFL rosters, led by Los Angeles Rams star and reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett. "What a great accomplishment for those guys yesterday," Elko said.

Cleveland Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion won the team's Maurice Bassett Award, which is awarded to the best Browns rookie in training camp. The former Texas A&M playmaker was a first round pick in the 2026 draft.

Texas A&M will unveil a new R.C. Slocum statue outside Kyle Field at 2 p.m. Friday. Slocum coached the Aggies from 1989 to 2002, finishing with a 123-47-2 record. "Really, really unbelievable accomplishment for a guy who is the winningest head football coach in Texas A&M history, a guy who won six Southwest Conference championships, two Big 12 South Conference championships, and then really a guy who epitomizes what being an elite coach here at Texas A&M is all about," Elko said. "Hopefully we'll get a lot of people out for that."

There's more to Houston with the Chronicle.

title: Under-17s draw on debut at the Youth Club World Cup
description: This Monday (31), the Tricolor U-17 side drew in the opening round of the Youth Club World Cup in Spain. At Campo Villanueva de Córdoba, in Villanueva, Spain, the team drew 2-2 with GNK Dinamo Zagreb...
fullText:
This Monday (31), the Tricolor U-17 side drew in the opening round of the Youth Club World Cup in Spain. At Campo Villanueva de Córdoba, in Villanueva, Spain, the team drew 2-2 with GNK Dinamo Zagreb, with goals from Brenno and Robert.

São Paulo started better and opened the scoring in the fourth minute after Brenno won a penalty and converted it. In the eighth minute, the opponent equalized, but Tricolor quickly went back in front through Robert, who finished well to score in the 13th minute. Even with the lead, the São Paulo side coached by Alexandre Torrezan pressed high on the opponent's buildup and showed attacking strength in the final third as it looked to extend the advantage.

In the second half, the style of play remained the same, but the opponent managed to break the pressure and equalized in the 38th minute.

In the penalty shootout for the extra point, the São Paulo side was beaten 3-2.

The next match takes place this Wednesday (2), when Tricolor faces Sporting at 3 p.m. in Palma del Río, and the very next day it closes out the first phase against Málaga, also at 3 p.m., in Cabra.

title: Mitchell Tinsley is quickly picked up by Texans
description: The former Bengals receiver gets another shot.
fullText:
Mitchell Tinsley was perhaps the most uplifting story out of the Cincinnati Bengals' 2025 training camp.

The undrafted receiver made acrobatic catch after acrobatic catch in practice and the preseason to earn a spot on the roster and the opportunity to play in the regular season.

He went on to play in all 17 regular season games and get eight receptions for 116 yards and two touchdowns.

Introducing Mitchell Tinsley!

JAXvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+https://t.co/HkKw7uXVnt pic.twitter.com/cGZdTH7FtR

But then another underdog, Dohnte Meyers, made the roster yesterday, as did fourth-rounder Colbie Young out of Georgia. All of a sudden, there was no longer a need for Tinsley's abilities.

But less than a day after he was cut by the Bengals, Tinsley was signed to the Houston Texans' practice squad.

#Texans signing former #Bengals #Commanders receiver Mitchell Tinsley to practice squad, per league source. Eight career catches, 116 yards, two touchdowns pic.twitter.com/A5VHbRjGdh

The good news is that Tinsley could end up being a major contributor in Houston, where they've struggled to find good role playing receivers.

In the end, it's a win-win for a Bengals team that might finally have their WR3 and Tinsley, who deserves the chance to be on the field to make eye-popping plays.

title: What Commanders GM Adam Peters, HC Dan Quinn said after 53-man roster cuts
description: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters spoke publicly after forming the 53-man roster
fullText:
Commanders head coach Dan Quinn and general manager Adam Peters spoke to the media on Monday afternoon, following the formation of their initial 53-man roster and practice squad.

They discussed why players were kept and others were let go, also providing updates on a number of key players dealing with injury.

Good news was provided about some key players, including center Nick Allegretti's return to practice on Monday.

Peters and Quinn also gave some updates on edge rusher Odafe Oweh and explained why cornerback Trey Amos was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return.

Here are some highlights from that important press conference as the Commanders turn toward the 2026 regular season:

Back at practice today: Nick Allegretti, Marcus Mariota, Daron Payne, Jordan Magee, Ben Sinnott.

Adam Peters: "Really pleased with where we are, how we competed in camp and where we ended up."

Peters says the team has added free agents, which will be released soon. Said they are "far from done" with roster moves

Dan Quinn said they're "still working through where they're at at center."

Quinn said he loves the amount of work Cosmi and Conerly got together as well as Paul and Coleman. Both he and Peters stressed the importance of getting Allegretti back. Peters: “We have a ton of confidence in him.”

Adam Peters on center: we have a ton of confidence in Nick and he's had 3000 snaps in the NFL and Matt (Gulbin) has passed all those test we've asked of him and think he has a bright future.

Dan Quinn on figuring out center what has he seen from other guys – Matt Gulbin, sometimes with the rookies you see the progress, you see his strength but you don't see him repeating mistakes. Julian Good Jones playing as much as he did this camp, it'll pay dividends getting all…

Dan Quinn says "it's not ideal" that Jayden Daniels didnt get work with Nick Allegretti during training camp but the team "can only control what they can control"

What went into the moves in February at center from Adam Peters: I don't want to go back and talk about Tyler (Biadasz), but were confident in Nick and thought he'd be our starter and we don't want to go back with who we got or didn't get and rewrite the history of six months ago

Adam Peters on Trey Amos: "Want to take it slow with him"

Could Amos be back in a few weeks? "Maybe"

On Odafe Oweh: Dan Quinn said he won't practice today but he's "making a lot of progress. As we get into next week, thrilled he's making this kind of progress to get ready."

Did not say he'll play in the opener, but will know more when he returns.

I asked Adam Peters how many years does being a draft pick buy a player?

Adam Peters: "none"

Adam Peters mentions arm talent and moxie talking about Athan Kaliakmanis, "he made a lot of big throws…he's not afraid to rip it"

Dan Quinn told reporters that CB Fabian Moreau is re-joining the Commanders. He'll fortify a CB corps that was untenably thin on the initial 53. Always figured that move was coming.

Dan Quinn on Jayden Daniels' readiness: It's been excellent for him

Commanders gave up 160 rushing yards a game through the preseason. Quinn says they didn't show everything in the preseason, so not worried about a repeat of those performances

Adam Peters: "Obviously our fans are passionate and you love to have passionate fans; that's great. Bu there is a lot of stuff we're doing here that maybe they don’t see and a lot of things I'm excited to see in a couple weeks."

Adam Peters: want to develop Jaden Bradley on practice squad. AP thinks Bradley has a future in this league.

Adam Peters says he's very confident in this team for this season. Says the Commanders have shown very little of what will be out there come Week 1

title: Notre Dame QB CJ Carr's brother Tommy gets a key role at Michigan
description: Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr's brother Tommy will be the backup QB at Michigan to start 2026.
fullText:
Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr's brother is going to be the backup quarterback for one of the Fighting Irish's historic rivals.

Tommy Carr will be the QB2 for the University of Michigan Wolverines, according to head coach Kyle Whittingham.

Former Michigan head coach Lloyd Carr is the brothers' grandfather, and CJ made quite a stir by choosing to play in South Bend.

It's too bad that the Notre Dame-Michigan rivalry is on an indefinite hiatus -- it would be pretty cool to have a brother-versus-brother game, even if one is, at least for now, the backup coming off the bench.

title: High school football top 10: De La Salle maintains top spot after beating Serra
description: Quarterback Jaxon Loftin passed for three touchdowns as De La Salle backed up its preseason No. 1 ranking with a season-opening win over then-No. 2 Serra, plus other big outcomes from the first week.
fullText:
The one supposed question mark for De La Salle's top-ranked football team turned out to be an exclamation point in Friday's season-opening 35-25 win at No. 2 Serra on Friday night.

Jaxon Loftin, a 5-foot-10, 180-pound senior quarterback, was all smiles after he completed 12 of 18 passes for 196 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 38 

Loftin also saw another potential TD pass dropped and rushed for another score that was curiously taken away when the referees ruled Serra was offside but didn't stop the play.

Nevertheless, Loftin was definitely the game's most pleasant - and upbeat - surprise considering the Spartans had speed, brawn, Division I talent at all other positions coming in. His job was presumably to just manage the game and not make mistakes. He did so much more.

"I did, I really did," he said with a giant grin and an unapologetic "ah shucks" shake of the head. "It was truly a blessing. I'm just so proud of everyone and just how much work we've put in since January."

De La Salle's No. 1 threat Duece Jones-Drew, a UCLA commit, backed up his high ranking, especially after halftime when he had three touchdowns on a 30-yard catch and TD jaunts of 27 and 18 yards. He said Loftin's positive personality in the huddle helped key the second-half turnaround, wiping out a 17-14 halftime deficit.

"I love Jaxon," Jones-Drew said. "I mean, he's so competitive in the weight room, on the field. He pushes everybody around him to be better too. … He makes sure we have that chemistry. He's always happy, even in the huddle. Like after a bad play, he's all smiles, picking everybody up."

Friday, it wasn't just with his attitude. On the second play from scrimmage, he fired a 47-yard completion to state Damari Dean and six plays later on fourth down, they hooked up on a 9-yard touchdown. Later in the half he fired a 35-yard TD pass to Dylan Scott. "That first completion helped give all of us a lot of confidence, myself included," Loftin said.

Said De La Salle coach Justin Alumbaugh of Loftin: "He's got a lot of pizazz. He's just a 'love-life' type of kid. There are always things to work on but for his first start, I think he did a great job. He moved the team well and made some big plays for us."

Here's the Chronicle's Top 10 after week one.

1. De La Salle (1-0, #1 last week): Jones-Drew was held to 25 yards rushing in the first half but finished with 18 carries for 84 yards. He broke several tackles en route to his game-clinching score with 1:45 remaining. Linebackers Jmo Mitzel and Landon Miller had eight tackles each and  Prayshawn Harang had two of the team's four sacks. Next: Friday versus Cardinal Newman-Santa Rosa (0-1).

2. Pittsburg (1-0, #3): JaVale Jones threw one touchdown pass to Deveon Wilson and another to Kenneth Ward as the Pirates scored the game's final 34 points in a 40-7 home win over Monterey Trail-Elk Grove. Isaiah Harrison, Isaiah Davis and Ahsoni Seals all rushed for TDs. Next: Friday vs. St. John Bosco-Bellflower (1-1).

3. Serra (0-1, #2): A rash of injuries and leg cramping against De La Salle hurt the Padres, who got a 68-yard touchdown run by Cal-bound Jeovanni Henley, two touchdown passes by Caleb Bandel - one each to Hugh Ford and Charlie Walsh - and a 47-yard field goal by Tristan Aspinall. Next: Friday at Kahuku-Hawaii (3-0).

4. Cardinal Newman (0-1, #4): The Cardinals took host Folsom to overtime before falling 23-17 last week. Cardinal Newman, which led 10-0, had a chance to win in regulation but a 32-yard field-goal attempt with 30 seconds left was blocked. A 99-yard kickoff return by Folsom's CJ Wallace also hurt the Cardinals, who got touchdowns from James Curoso and Owen Grafe. Next: Friday at De La Salle (1-0).

Junior tailback Owen Power rushed for 127 yards and two touchdowns, and Cole Dawes threw for two scores as the visiting Wolves had no trouble breezing past defending state 4-A champion El Cerrito 41-14. Next: Friday at Enochs-Modesto (0-1).

6. Acalanes-Lafayette (1-0, #6): A 28-point spree in the second quarter wiped out a 14-7 deficit and the defense did the rest in a 35-14 win over Mitty at Foothill College-Los Altos Hills. Tyler Winkles completed 24 of 35 passes for 343 yards and five touchdowns, two each to Finn Rivera (seven catches, 114 yards) and Jackson Boselli (3, 116). Next: Friday at Menlo-Atherton (0-1).

7. Riordan (0-1, #5): UNLV-bound running back Adonyae Brown was held to 33 yards on 14 carries, but did have a 92-yard TD reception from Jayden Crane in a 21-13 loss at West-Salt Lake City, which improved to 3-0. Frank Ennix and Soape Mafuahingano each had five QB hurries for the Crusaders. Next: Friday vs. Clayton Valley Charter-Concord (0-1)

8. St. Ignatius (1-0, #8): Sophomore Isaac Liu threw for 229 yards and three touchdowns, one to Luke Tribolet, who also rushed for 67 yards and another score as the Wildcats beat host San Marin-Novato 42-7. The Wildcats rushed for 240 yards, with Max Gines going for 82 and a TD. Next: Friday vs. Marin Catholic-Kentfield (0-1).

9. St. Francis (1-0, #9): Luke Mota rushed 13 times for 102 yards including a 54-yard touchdown and Drew Cumby threw for 174 yards and two scores and added 88 yards rushing, including an 80-yard TD run, leading the Lancers to a 31-23 home win over Manteca. Cody Butler and Uate Pifeleti had touchdown catches. Next: Friday vs. Del Oro-Loomis (1-0).

10. Bishop O'Dowd-Oakland (1-0, #13): In the coaching debut of Majett Whiteside, the defending 5-AA state champions had little trouble in a 55-6 home win over Castlemont-Oakland. The Dragons rushed for nearly 350 yards, getting 110 yards and three TDs from Bryan Edwards. Next: Friday at Mater Dei Catholic-San Diego.

Week 1 notes: Justin Fung completed 13 of 18 passes for 220 yards and six touchdowns as Palo Alto, which went 0-10 last season, opened with a 56-14 win over Leigh-San Jose in the head coaching debut of Edward Tonga. … DJ Hicks rushed 12 times for 215 yards and three touchdowns, leading Oakland to a 34-20 home win over Del Norte-Crescent City. .. It was a tough opener for new McClymonds-Oakland coach Marcus Peters, whose team lost 50-0 in Hawaii to Mililani, which improved to 3-0. … Two-time defending state 7-A champion Balboa opened with a 38-6 home win over Mt. Diablo-Concord. … Foothill-Pleasanton's Amaree Hill rushed 15 times for 205 yards and three touchdowns in a 28-6 win over Newark Memorial. … Camden Camara rushed 27 times for 190 yards and a TD and Leysen Rodrigues passed for 311 yards and three scores in Liberty-Brentwood's 32-21  win over preseason No. 15 California-San Ramon. … Tennyson-Hayward's Cedric Whitaker III, Redwood Christian-San Lorenzo's Elijah Simmons and Novato's Diego Sacche each rushed for three touchdowns in opening wins. … Brody Zirelli threw for 217 yards and three touchdowns, two to Austin Sotto, in Carlmont-Belmont's 25-7 win over visiting Menlo School-Atherton in the head coaching debut of Antoine Evans, who coached the previous  four seasons at Sacred Heart Cathedral. ... Under new coach Darius Bell, Sacred Heart Cathedral opened with a 42-10 win at Rancho Cotate-Rohnert Park behind three TD pass from Michael Vasquez.

There's more to San Francisco with the Chronicle.

title: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: What Arteta and Saka said
description: Saka scored in consecutive Premier League appearances for the first time since November 2024, with all three of his goals in the competition against Villa coming at Villa Park.  Arsenal have now started their Premier League season with two wins in a row for the seventh time in the last eight seasons, including the last five in a row.
fullText:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta speaking to Match of the Day: "This is a really difficult place to come and win the game. Last season we lost in the last kick of the game. They were hurt after what happened last week. It was a great squad performance tonight."

On if this is his best team in terms of strength in depth: "That is what we need. The players that come in make the difference. All of them contributed to create more dominance and more momentum.

"The level of focus and the way they want to contribute to the team, that is going to be decisive in the season."

Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka, speaking to Sky Sports: "Very, very tough game. It's not easy coming here, they made it hard for us. It feels even better to come out with the win.

"The way they defend, really compact and with a high line, they caught us offside. We had to adapt to that. Different from what we faced last week, we weren't able to implement our attacking pattern.

"One goal is normally enough for us because we are so solid at the back. When we got the first one, it actually opened the game up. We wanted to push for the second one.

"All the full-backs, the way they play gives us a lot. For us wingers, it opens up the game for us, we've always got composure in the box.

"We weren't at our highest level with the ball. Without it, we were incredible. As soon as we lost it, we were running back. We knew that they liked to play in transition.

"All the boys put in a shift tonight. It helps with a clean sheet."

Saka scored in consecutive Premier League appearances for the first time since November 2024, with all three of his goals in the competition against Villa coming at Villa Park.

Arsenal have now started their Premier League season with two wins in a row for the seventh time in the last eight seasons, including the last five in a row.

title: Chargers reunion: Caleb Murphy signing to practice squad
description: The Los Angeles Chargers reunite with familiar edge rusher Caleb Murphy.
fullText:
The Chargers have added a familiar face to their edge rusher room, signing Caleb Murphy to their practice squad.

Murphy was recently waived by the Giants after failing to make their initial 53-man roster.

The Giants claimed Murphy off waivers in mid-December 2025. The 26-year-old signed a reserve/future contract with New York in March 2026.

Before Murphy's time with the Giants, he played for the Chargers and was part of their organization in 2024 and 2025.

In late October 2024, Murphy signed to the Chargers' practice squad and eventually signed a reserve/future contract with Los Angeles in January 2025.

Murphy played in six games for the Chargers in 2025 and recorded 12 tackles, one quarterback hit, and 0.5 sacks, while establishing himself as a reliable asset on special teams units.

He finished the 2025 season with the Patriots, where he played in five games.

title: Liverpool confirm departure of midfielder but Gakpo looks set to stay
description: Stefan Bajcetic has completed a permanent move from Liverpool to Celta Vigo, bringing an end to his five-and-a-half-year spell with the Reds.The 21-year-old midfielder returns to the Spanish club for ...
fullText:
Stefan Bajcetic has completed a permanent move from Liverpool to Celta Vigo, bringing an end to his five-and-a-half-year spell with the Reds.

The 21-year-old midfielder returns to the Spanish club for around £1m, having made 22 senior appearances and scored once for the Anfield side.

Bajcetic's departure could mark one of Liverpool's final pieces of transfer business before the window closes, following the signing of Bradley Barcola.

Cody Gakpo now looks increasingly likely to remain at Anfield, meanwhile.

Manchester City had made an offer for the Netherlands international, with Spurs also having been keen.

title: Steelers GM confirms Max Hurleman, Lew Nichols and more practice squad signings
description: The Steelers kept all 10 of their NFL draft picks on the initial 53-man roster, forcing some demotions for some veteran players.
fullText:
More than a dozen players who practiced and played with the Pittsburgh Steelers during training camp and the preseason will be sticking around.

GM Omar Khan confirmed a list of 13 players signed to the team's practice squad as of the afternoon of Monday, Aug. 31.

It includes: Running backs Lew Nichols and Travis Homer; receivers Max Hurleman and Brandon Smith; tight end Lake McRee; offensive linemen Doug Nester and Steven Jones; defensive linemen Esezi Otomewo and Kyler Baugh; cornerback Doneiko Slaughter; safety Sebastian Castro; and linebackers Jacoby Windmon and Julius Welschof.

Required reading: Steelers keep both Drew Allar, Will Howard behind Aaron Rodgers, Mason Rudolph at QB

The Steelers cut all of them from the active roster ahead of the NFL's Sunday deadline to reduce roster sizes to the standard 53 players. The team can still add up to four more names to the practice squad before finalizing the group ahead of Week 1, when they face the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13 at Acrisure Stadium. They will get an exemption for an extra spot because Welschof is an international pathway player.

Nicols and Homer led the backfield in two of three preseason games but were squeezed out of the active roster by rookie Eli Heidenreich, the team's seventh-round selection who also has utility on special teams. He'll be the lone backup behind top backs Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle for now.

Hurleman was a standout with 99 total receiving yards through the three contests against the Green Bay Packers, New York Jets and Buffalo Bills. He gave way to rookie Kaden Wetjen, who's the lead kick returner on special teams, as well as Ben Skowronek, a Pro Bowl selection for his special teams play last season.

McRee opened some eyes working mostly with the backup quarterbacks. He caught a 38-yard pass from Drew Allar in the loss to the Jets on Aug. 21, then added a touchdown from Will Howard in the finale.

Defensively, Welschof had two sacks in the exhibition campaign.

Injuries will be the main factor in any of these players getting called up to the active roster at some point this season. Hurleman, Hurleman and Nichols would be most likely to earn promotions if rookies like Heidenreich and Wetjen struggle to find their footing.

title: The Montreal Canadiens Can Expect More Stability in Net
description: The Montreal Canadiens had a successful season culminating in an Eastern Conference Final appearance. Before next season, several questions remain about Montreal’s goaltending. What role does Samuel Montembeault have on the Canadiens moving forward? Will the two young goaltenders, Jakub Dobeš and Jacob Fowler, have the stamina to withstand 84 regular-season games and get the […] The post The Montreal Canadiens Can Expect More Stability in Net appeared first on The Lead.
fullText:
The Montreal Canadiens had a successful season culminating in an Eastern Conference Final appearance. Before next season, several questions remain about Montreal's goaltending.

What role does Samuel Montembeault have on the Canadiens moving forward? Will the two young goaltenders, Jakub Dobeš and Jacob Fowler, have the stamina to withstand 84 regular-season games and get the Canadiens to the playoffs? Will new goalie coach Marco Marciano make a meaningful difference?

Despite these questions, one thing is certain: the Montreal Canadiens will have a better presence in net this season.

Samuel Montembeault was the Canadiens' starting goaltender in the 2025-2026 season. This season was not his strongest performance. In the 2024-2025 regular season, Montembeault had a .902 save percentage and won 31 out of his 62 starts. Compared to this year, Montembeault posted an .872 average save percentage and only won 10 of his 25 starts. In 15 of these starts, Montembeault posted a save percentage below .850.

This performance, along with a series of losses, was one reason Jacob Fowler was called up from the Canadiens' AHL team, the Laval Rocket. For several months, the Habs rolled with a nontraditional three-goalie rotation. This rotation allowed Canadiens management to decide on their playoff and future tandem, which does not include Montembeault.

Whether Montreal holds on to Montembeault or determines a new destination for him, it is clear that he will not be the starter this season.

Another factor that bodes well for the Habs' future in net is 22-year-old goaltender Jacob Fowler. Fowler thrived playing for the Laval Rocket. Before being called up, Fowler had 19 wins in 27 starts, three shutouts, and an exceptional .916 save percentage. When he was called up to the Canadiens, Fowler was equally impressive in his first appearances, posting a .908 save percentage.

Fowler proved his worth to the Canadiens when he was called up on March 11 and, hours later, thrown into a key divisional game against the Ottawa Senators. This game came down to one goal and a nail-biting final minute, in which Fowler faced eight shot attempts and five shots on goal. In this moment, Fowler earned the first star of the game and the trust of the Canadiens organization.

His calm demeanor and skill make him the league's top goalie prospect.

In addition to Jacob Fowler, the Canadiens have Jakub Dobeš. Dobeš was one of the most exciting goalies to watch during this year's playoffs. Beyond his high skill level, Dobeš proved he can win games while playing with intensity. Dobeš took four penalties this postseason, the most out of any goalie in the league.

In addition to his attitude, his numbers in the playoffs speak for themselves. In 19 games, Dobeš averaged a .908 save percentage. Dobeš won 9 of his 19 games, with the team finally falling in Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Final. In this impressive run, Dobeš started every game. He also won back-to-back Game 7s, posting an exceptional .966 and a .949 in each game, respectively.

In addition to this, it was Dobeš' exceptional regular-season play at the beginning of April, an eight-game win streak in which Dobeš played five, that led to the Canadiens clinching their playoff spot. He will undoubtedly be the tender the Canadiens rely on most next season, especially under their new goalie coach.

Marco Marciano replaced Éric Raymond as Canadiens goalie coach in late January. Marciano had been with the Rocket since 2017 before he was promoted to the main club for his repeated success with all three goalies. This hiring change significantly bumped the team's save percentage from .879 to a steady .908 for the remainder of the season.

To Fowler and Dobeš's advantage, goalie coach Marco Marciano will be with them for an entire season instead of just half, improving stability in the crease.

Having two young goaltenders, on what is already the youngest team in the league, puts the Canadiens in a unique position. What this tandem may lack in experience, they make up for in talent, work ethic, and composure.

Hockey Hall of Famer and retired Habs goaltender Carey Price commented on the young goalies, saying, "I really love Dobeš' compete level; he's got that 'grrr' in his game, he's got that swagger. I really enjoy watching that. Fowler kind of reminds me more of myself, a little more reserved." Dobeš and Fowler's styles complement each other.

Tune in to see the Habs season start on September 29, 2026, at 7 pm EST.

The post The Montreal Canadiens Can Expect More Stability in Net appeared first on The Lead.

title: Browns WR KC Concepcion wins Maurice Bassett award
description: The first rounder wins the award for best rookie in training camp.
fullText:
Last year's Cleveland Browns offense lacked playmakers who could make things happen after the catch. As a result, the team wasn't very creative or explosive through the air, aside from Harold Fannin Jr., who was fantastic as a rookie after the catch.

General manager Andrew Berry knew this had to change, and that played a part in the team drafting wide receiver KC Concepcion in the first round. Now, with the regular season just around the corner and training camp in the books, Concepcion has been awarded the Maurice Bassett Award by the media for the most outstanding rookie of training camp this year.

Concepcion absolutely deserved this award; you couldn't go to a Browns training camp practice this year without seeing him make several head-turning plays at every practice he was a part of. If the Browns offense is going to be better and more explosive this year, he will play a big part in it improving with his explosiveness and ability to create in the open field.

title: Raphinha & Lamine Yamal score twice in Barca win
description: Raphinha and Lamine Yamal both score twice as Barcelona beat Rayo Vallecano to make it three wins out of three in La Liga.
fullText:
Barcelona 5 - 2 Rayo Vallecano FT

Raphinha and Lamine Yamal both scored twice as Barcelona beat Rayo Vallecano to make it three wins out of three in La Liga.

Brazil's Raphinha is the first player to score five goals in the first three La Liga games of a season since Lionel Messi for Barcelona in 2017.

Those games have all come in eight days with Barca cramming their fixtures in after starting late because of the amount of World Cup players in their squad.

Rayo actually led through Sergio Camello's tidy first-time effort, but Raphinha levelled after some good footwork before slotting into the bottom corner.

Lamine Yamal then blasted a piledriver in from just inside the box to put Barca ahead.

Florian Lejeune then turned fellow former Newcastle player Anthony Gordon's cross into his own net.

Camello's header give Rayo hope again but England forward Gordon's backheel found Raphinha to make it 4-2.

Spain teenager Lamine Yamal added a fifth in injury time - his 51st goal for Barcelona - with a cushioned effort into the bottom corner from 20 yards.

Barca and Real Madrid are the only two teams on nine points, while Rayo Vallecano have just one point.

title: See 7 of Naomi Osaka’s Best Tennis Outfits Over the Years
description: The tennis star often wears looks inspired by her Japanese heritage
fullText:
Naomi Osaka is known for making an entrance when it comes to her match day outfits.

The tennis star, who is currently ranked world No. 13 by the WTA, has become just as famous for her style as she has for her athletic prowess.

Osaka is from Osaka, Japan, and she frequently pays homage to her Japanese heritage with her outfits. The mom of one has even helped design some of her ensembles over the years.

"Sometimes people say athletes are in show business or entertainers or whatever," she said during a post-game press conference at the 2026 French Open, per Reuters. "For me, Grand Slam walk-ons are the only time that I possibly feel like I'm an entertainer."

From the US Open to Wimbledon, here's a look at seven times Naomi Osaka served serious style on the tennis court.

In 2024, Osaka made her triumphant return to the US Open after going on maternity leave in a green and white ensemble designed by Yooh Ahn and Nike.

Worn by Osaka during her first-round singles match on day two of the tournament, the look featured a white windbreaker with a large green bow, a green tutu with white tulle ruffles and a matching green visor.

"The inspiration that fueled the look for me — and this might be a Japanese term — is feeling like a 'magical girl' on the court," Osaka told Nike at the time. "There's a moment of transformation for me when I walk onto the court, and I have a lot of fun playing, so wanting everyone who sees the outfit to connect with that feeling is a really big motivation for me."

The following year, Osaka stepped out at the 2025 French Open in another show-stopping Nike ensemble.

Rendered in blush pink, the tennis kit featured a layered ruffle skirt paired with a matching maroon-and-pink varsity jacket. Osaka's hair accessories were a nod to the Japanese comic Sailor Moon and her shoes were inspired by Japanese cherry blossoms, a.k.a. sakura.

"The shoes are sakura-themed, which is I guess just in time for spring, which is sakura season," Osaka said at the time, per Tennis.com. "It follows the flower story that we have throughout the year."

Osaka returned to the US Open in 2025 wearing a matching orange set from Nike that featured glittering mesh panels and a tiered bubble skirt. In a post-game press conference, she told reporters that planning her outfit for the match was a "little chaotic."

"It was really elaborate because the crystals are really hard to do on a performance outfit," Osaka said.

As for accessories, she paired the look with a bedazzled Labubu named "Billie Jean Bling" after tennis legend Billie Jean King.

Ahead of her first-round singles match on day three of the 2026 Australian Open, Osaka made an entrance in a jellyfish-inspired look designed by her and Robert Wun in collaboration with Nike.

The ensemble featured a white pleated skirt layered over matching pants, a blue-and-green textured minidress and a white wide-brim hat over which she draped a gauzy white veil. The athlete also carried a small white umbrella as she walked onto the court.

Osaka explained to Vogue at the time that the inspiration for the outfit came from a book she had read to her daughter, Shai. "There was an image of a jellyfish, and when I showed it to her she got so excited," she told the outlet.

Osaka embraced animal print at the 2026 BNP Paribas Open in a tennis dress designed by Nike. The one-piece look featured a cheetah pattern against a lime green backdrop. Osaka finished off the look with a black Nike visor.

Pre-match, the tennis star also sported some custom jewelry from Filipino-American designer Chris Habana, including ear cuffs and a gold mouthpiece.

"He's created these really layered pieces for artists that feel expressive, but also intentional," Osaka said of Habana in an interview with Vogue at the time. "I loved the idea of bringing that energy onto the court."

Osaka opted for another layered ensemble at the 2026 French Open. Stepping out on day three of the tournament, the athlete made a statement in a black corset and a floor-length black pleated skirt, both of which were designed by Swiss couturier Kevin Germanier.

She then shed her top layer to reveal a gold Nike tennis dress with a ruffled, sequined skirt.

"I feel like fashion, for me, I tell people, I don't talk a lot, so that way I can talk through my clothes," Osaka said in a press conference at the time. "That means I can be as loud with colors or patterns or fabric as I want."

Though Wimbledon has a strict all-white dress code, Osaka didn't let that stop her from getting creative. On day one of the tournament, the tennis star debuted a layered look inspired by a Japanese ceremonial dress: the kimono.

Osaka collaborated with Tokyo-based designer Hana Yagi on the ensemble, which was covered in embroidered cranes and cherry blossoms. She paired it with a long ruffled skirt, styling her hair with a traditional kanzashi hair ornament. Underneath, Osaka wore an all-white Nike tennis kit.

During an on-court interview after her match, Osaka also revealed the pop culture inspiration behind the look: Quentin Tarantino's Kill Bill.

"I was thinking about my favorite movies. I love Kill Bill, and then I remembered absolutely falling in love with Lucy Liu's character, and she has an all-white kimono. I remember thinking that was really cool and amazing," she said, per Reuters and WTA Tennis.

title: Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: What Emery said
description: Aston Villa have lost their first two Premier League matches of the season for the first time since 2019-20.  Since Opta began recording shot data in 2003-04, Aston Villa are just the second team to fail to have a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season, along with Swansea City in 2017-18 who were later relegated that season.
fullText:
Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, speaking to Match of the Day: "We performed like we planned and we competed like we planned. We didn't achieve the result, of course, it's painful. But through how we played and competed, that is the way we want to build again, to build a team like we want. The debut of some players was fantastic."

On if is excited to work with new players: "We are happy how we are closing the transfer window. We are not regretting anything. The players we have joining should be enough to build the team again with the structure we want."

On Taylor Harwood-Bellis watching in the stands: "I don't know if it's official, hopefully we can close everything. We did a fantastic job in the last three years, now with the new chapter, try to rebuild the team as fast as possible."

On last year's success despite a slow start and if people are quick to forget that: "Each year is different. We have an idea in our mind to build again and create a new chapter. We have lost two matches. We don't want to compare with the past, we must focus on this year."

Aston Villa have lost their first two Premier League matches of the season for the first time since 2019-20. They are the first team to finish in the top-four of the top-flight (4th in 2025-26) and then lose their first two games of the following season since both Arsenal and Manchester United in 1992-93, and first to do so without scoring since QPR in 1976-77.

Since Opta began recording shot data in 2003-04, Aston Villa are just the second team to fail to have a shot on target in their first two Premier League matches in a season, along with Swansea City in 2017-18 who were later relegated that season.

title: Analyst says 2nd Super Bowl puts Matthew Stafford in top-5 QB debate
description: Dan Orlovsky will be ready to beat the drum of Matthew Stafford's legacy if the Rams quarterback wins another Super Bowl.
fullText:
Dan Orlovsky has never shied away from beating the drum for Matthew Stafford. The former NFL quarterback and current ESPN analyst has spent years arguing that his ex-teammate's raw arm talent, elite pocket processing, and fourth-quarter heroics put him in a higher echelon than mainstream national narratives often suggest.

Now, Orlovsky is setting the bar even higher for the Los Angeles Rams' veteran signal-caller.

During a recent appearance on ESPN's Get Up, Orlovsky dropped a bold assessment regarding how another Lombardi Trophy would impact Stafford's historical legacy.

"[If] Matthew Stafford gets another one, he has an MVP in his back pocket; he becomes top five, top seven quarterback of all-time conversation," Orlovsky claimed.

"Matthew Stafford gets another one, he has an MVP in his back pocket, he becomes top-five, top-seven of all-time conversation" – Dan Orlovsky pic.twitter.com/aRggw5hYgY

Stafford's statistical foundation is already built for Canton. He currently ranks among the top 10 quarterbacks in NFL history in passing yards and passing touchdowns and is still one of the elite players in the leage as he heads into season No. 17 at the age of 38.

What long held Stafford back in all-time discussions was postseason success during his twelve seasons with the Detroit Lions. But after being traded to Los Angeles in 2021, Stafford immediately flipped that narrative by winning a Super Bowl in his first season with the Rams and making it back to the playoffs in three of the past four years as well.

Adding a second Super Bowl ring—and potentially a Super Bowl MVP to pair with his regular-season hardware—would put Stafford in extraordinarily rare company. Only a small fraternity of quarterbacks in NFL history have won multiple Super Bowl titles while ranking inside the top 10 for major volume passing records.

Now, there is a difference between a Hall of Fame resume, which Stafford has now, and a top-five or top-seven conversation. Placing Stafford ahead of legends like Joe Montana, Peyton Manning, Johnny Unitas, or Tom Brady in a consensus top-five list will certainly provoke fiery debate on sports talk radio.

However, if Sean McVay's offense delivers another championship with No. 9 at the helm, the debate will certainly rage on.

title: Zimbabwe survive huge Namibia scare, clinch five-run win in final-over thriller
description: In a nail-biting finish, Zimbabwe triumphed over Namibia by a mere five runs. After struggling initially, Namibia showcased an impressive fightback, highlighted by a pivotal seventh-wicket partnership that nearly led them to victory. Yet, Zimbabwe's bowlers maintained their composure in the dying moments to clinch the match, adding to this excitement following Namibia's fantastic earlier display against South Africa.
fullText:
Zimbabwe survived a stunning late fightback from Namibia to pull off a thrilling five-run victory in Windhoek, recovering from a precarious 101/6 to post 195/6 before holding their nerve in a dramatic final over.

Namibia, who had opened the tri-series with an impressive win over South Africa, looked out of the contest at 76/6 during their chase. But Zane Green and Alexander Volschenk produced a breathtaking 109-run seventh-wicket partnership off just 49 balls to put Namibia within touching distance of another remarkable victory.

Zimbabwe eventually held on, with Brad Evans delivering the decisive final over to seal a result that looked highly unlikely midway through the chase.

Asked to bat first, Zimbabwe made an aggressive start through Ben Curran and Brian Bennett, who put on 64 for the opening wicket. Namibia struck with the final ball of the Powerplay when Bennett top-edged a pull off JJ Smit to deep midwicket for 32 off 21 balls.

Dion Myers fell to Bernard Scholtz in the following over, before Gerhard Erasmus produced the biggest breakthrough by dismissing Sikandar Raza for a golden duck. Curran was then removed in the ninth over, and Erasmus struck again soon after to send back Wesley Madhavere.

Zimbabwe had slumped to 79/5 in the 10th over and were in danger of being bowled out cheaply. But Ryan Burl and Brad Evans turned the innings around with a crucial 94-run partnership off 48 balls.

Namibia's decision to return to spin for the final over proved particularly expensive. Burl smashed Erasmus for a six and three consecutive fours, taking 20 from the over as Zimbabwe surged to 195/6.

Namibia's chase began with early pressure from Zimbabwe. Louren Steenkamp was dismissed by Blessing Muzarabani in the third over, while Erasmus made 12 before falling to Brad Evans.

Loftie-Eaton briefly counterattacked with 20 off 13, but Brian Bennett then struck twice in three balls to leave Namibia at 66/4. Frylinck's 22 off 29 was unable to halt the slide, and when Ruben Trumpelmann fell to Sikandar Raza, Namibia were reeling at 76/6.

Then came the extraordinary recovery.

Volschenk attacked the bowling from the outset, hitting Wellington Masakadza for two sixes in the 13th over. Green joined him, and the pair combined power with sharp running to keep Namibia's hopes alive.

Their partnership raced past 100, leaving Namibia needing only 16 from the final over with four wickets still in hand.

Evans began the last over with a no-ball, but Namibia could take only two runs from it. Green was then run out for 54 off 26 after being caught short at the non-striker's end by a direct hit from Raza.

Volschenk kept Namibia alive with a boundary but was dismissed for 56 off 29 when he edged a full, wide delivery, with wicketkeeper Tadiwanashe Marumani taking a superb one-handed catch.

With two balls remaining, Namibia needed nine. Scholtz was run out attempting a desperate single before Evans held his nerve to bowl Jack Brassell for a duck and complete Zimbabwe's five-run victory.

title: Run local embedder for 0.24% of the OpenAI price
description: Why semantic-search quality depends on the model, language, and corpus — and how Dzen Chat lets you run a local model or switch providers.
fullText:
Choosing an embedding model determines which documents search finds before a
language model begins writing an answer. A general-purpose model offered by a
large provider is convenient for getting started. But it is not necessarily the
best at understanding Russian, the language of a particular country,
specialist vocabulary, or a mixed corpus of instructions, contracts, and code.

For example, a visitor writes, “When will my purchase arrive?”, while the right
help-centre section is called “Delivery times and methods”. Keyword search may
miss that connection. Semantic search can find it — but only if the model maps
these particular phrasings well enough.

An embedding is a numerical vector through which a model represents the meaning
of a short piece of text. Phrases with similar meanings receive nearby vectors.
That lets a question about delivery match a section about timeframes even when
they share almost no words.

A model has at least four important properties: the languages it was trained
and evaluated on; its ability to distinguish similar but different intents; the
length of the text it can process; and its vector size and speed. A model
trained specifically on texts and queries in the relevant language can map its
phrasing, morphology, and shades of meaning more accurately than a generic
model from an external provider. The same applies to models for law, medicine,
code, or another field: they can make finer distinctions between similar
specialist concepts.

This matters especially for Russian-language and multilingual knowledge bases.
You can compare a general external model with a specialised model trained for
the relevant language group and see a practical difference: the right section
appears in the top results more often, while a similar but wrong page ranks
lower. That increases the chance that an answer is grounded in the right source.

Embedding quality affects not the wording of an answer, but which evidence
reaches its context in the first place. Weak matching produces three typical
errors: the needed fragment is not found; a similar but incorrect fragment ranks
higher; or search does not understand the user’s language and the organisation’s
terminology.

That is why it is only fair to call one model “better” after testing it on a
representative set of questions. Public leaderboard rank is not the only metric:
top-result accuracy, the share of answers with valid evidence, latency, and
vector size also matter.

External API prices per 1 million input tokens:

For an estimate, take a 500-token fragment. In the dzen_embedder benchmark, a
GTX 1080 processed about 248 fragments per second. Running continuously, that
is up to 640 million fragments, or about 320 billion tokens per month. This is
a theoretical ceiling: longer fragments and a real mixed workload reduce
throughput.

That monthly volume would cost roughly:

Conclusion. A server with an entry-level GPU at $100 per month can pay for
itself under sustained high utilisation: even the theoretical ceiling costs
thousands of dollars per month through an external API. In practice, calculate
this using your own data volume and workload. A local model is also chosen for
security: documents and embedding requests remain in your infrastructure rather
than being sent to an external provider. It also lets you choose a model that
understands the language and terminology of your knowledge base better.

dzen_embedder is a standalone
embedding service for Dzen Chat. At startup, it downloads the selected model
from Hugging Face and accepts requests through
an OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint. The
MTEB Leaderboard, a public comparison of
embedding models, can help you identify candidates. The web application and
background jobs do not each load an additional copy of the model or compete for
one GPU’s memory.

The service has two queues. A visitor’s question goes to the interactive queue
and has strict priority. Indexing a large site or reindexing a knowledge base
runs in the background queue and uses idle capacity. A batch that has already
started is completed, but the next batch does not begin while user questions
are waiting.

Below is a measurement of load from 1 to 64 parallel connections, up to the
first error. A red cross marks the first level with an unsuccessful response.

Findings: GPU and Apple Silicon completed the mixed workload up to 64
connections without errors; the CPU had its first two timeouts at 64
connections. A standalone service with one model preserves priority for visitor
requests while background indexing waits for idle capacity.

A local service also shortens the network path. A question does not travel to a
remote provider and back; when the service runs near the application, the
request stays inside the local network. That reduces variable latency and keeps
request text out of an external service. Local deployment still requires you to
secure your own server, update the model, and monitor the queue.

Open the dzen_embedder repository
on GitHub and follow the instructions. Or copy this prompt into your agent:

The agent will request access to the server and deploy the service itself.

The project is released under the permissive 0BSD licence: you can use, modify,
and include it in your own products.

title: 18 month survey of unsecured Ollama servers and an unsolved mystery
description: Global survey over eighteen months of unsecured Ollama servers. What's running where and an unsolved mystery
fullText:
OllamaSpider scrapes Shodan and grabs endpoints on ports that were never Ollama. The
 other two feeds verify their hosts and do not carry this. Open Ollama servers are not
 mostly fake, and there are thousands of real ones. This is a claim about a specific set
 of hosts in a specific feed.

These hosts are live and responding. Something on each one answers
 the Ollama API with a model list, a version string, a chat reply. All of them advertise
 some subset of one small, fixed pool of old, unremarkable models
 (llama2:latest, llama3:latest, openchat:7b,
 qwen2.5:1.5b and a couple of others), frozen since early 2024, each at a
 size constant to the byte wherever it appears.

Ask one a question and the reply reads like
 filler from a small phrase bank rather than a model's answer. Ask its version and you get
 one of four fixed strings. Ask a model for its details and the response is empty, yet the
 running-model endpoint reports every one of them loaded and running at once, which no
 real host does.

Ask it to run a model that does not exist and it answers anyway; tell it
 to pull or delete a model and it reports success while nothing changes. Every command
 fails the same way: it always says yes. It is hundreds of hosts actively answering, and
 answering the same narrow way.

The sharpest test does not come from the scanners. In a fresh snapshot
 of 4,407 hosts that answer as Ollama, ollama version splits the
 population in two. Real servers report one of 172 different versions in a natural
 long tail. The responders return one of just four fixed strings, which stand as a tight
 near-equal band far above every real version. The four are in
 orange.

Hosts report a subset of the same handful of models, at sizes constant
 to the byte. The most common single catalogue in the feed, reported in full by tens of
 thousands of them, is:

Each model's size is constant to the byte, where genuinely pulled
 models vary by quantisation and version:

Spread across ports that mostly are not
 Ollama's. The same machine appears once per port:

Everything else here comes from commit logs. This does not. The project
 owner sent one instruction with a single correct answer to every OllamaSpider host
 advertising a given model and read the replies. A real model answers. A fake one replies
 with filler that quotes the prompt back.

Three runs, two test questions, three models
 from the fixed catalogue:

Line up all three probe captures and the replies give themselves away.
 Every one is an opener, then the word Regarding with your prompt quoted back,
 then a filler clause, then a closing question, each drawn from a tiny fixed pool.

Seven
 openers, eight middles, five closers make possible sentences,
 assembled by pre[rand] + your text + mid[rand] + post[rand]. This is string
 concatenation, not a model.

A real Ollama host reports one version. These return four fixed strings
 in near-equal proportion, from 0.1.0 to 0.6.3. It is the same
 rotate-a-fixed-list trick as the chat replies, applied to the version field.

Ollama listens on 11434. These hosts mostly do not. They answer on
 ports assigned to databases, service meshes and Windows remote management. This is the
 port mix of these responders, not of open Ollama servers in general.

ollama.com publishes the real blob size of every library tag, so a
 reported size can be checked against an outside fact. Each row is one host: the small
 dot is the tag's real published size, the large dot the size it reports for that tag.

Probing live hosts directly turned up a separate oddity. Hundreds of
 real, working Ollama boxes advertise a closed-weights model that cannot exist on
 Ollama: gpt-4, gpt-4o, claude-3-opus, and newer
 names like claude-opus-4.8, gpt-5.5 and
 gemini-3.5-flash. Of the live hosts we reached, 726 carried at least one
 of these.

They never appear alone. Every one of those 726 also runs genuine open
 models, usually Qwen, DeepSeek, or an abliterated Huihui build, so these are not empty
 decoys but real servers with fake names planted among the real ones. And the fake names
 carry no hf.co/ prefix the way the genuine models on the same boxes do, so
 they are made on the machine with ollama cp or a Modelfile, not pulled from
 Hugging Face. There is no upstream repo claiming to be GPT-4. It is local theatre.

Two very different levels of effort sit behind it. On 708 hosts the
 premium name points at a real but tiny 638 MB, 1.1B, Q4_0 llama blob, a small
 model wearing a big label. About 500 of them share one byte-identical blob, so this is a
 single artifact copied across hundreds of machines, not hundreds of separate pranks. A
 smaller, more deliberate seven fabricate the manifest outright: zero-byte entries whose
 parameter_size is the literal string synthetic, listing
 current premium models they demonstrably do not hold, each sitting beside per-host
 gateway-diagnostic entries. That tier looks like a catalogue kept
 up to date on purpose, or a scanner planting its own write-test marker. We cannot tell
 which from here.

One detail gives the game away: which names get faked. Whenever a real
 model actually sits behind the fake label, the label is a 2024 trophy, almost always
 gpt-4, gpt-4o or claude-3-opus. The current
 flagships, claude-opus-4.8 or gpt-5.5, turn up only as the
 empty synthetic manifests, never with weights behind them. So nobody parks a cheap model
 behind a current name and invites you to test it. The impersonation is frozen where it
 started, reaching for models that were the state of the art when these boxes were set up
 and have since been passed by weights anyone can download for free. Even the successful
 version of this lie now points at something a small open model would beat.

The fake names are not the only small thing on these boxes. Setting the
 fakes aside and measuring the real models, hosts carrying a premium name run
 noticeably smaller models than clean hosts: a median of 1.9 GB against 4.7 GB,
 with 42% under a gigabyte versus 16%. They also cluster on old Ollama versions, a fifth
 of them on 0.30.2 alone, where clean hosts spread across many including current
 releases. So the premium label tends to sit on an older, lighter, less maintained box.

Unknown, and the data does not let us pretend otherwise. What is
 established is narrow. Within OllamaSpider's feed, hundreds of live hosts answer the
 Ollama API with a frozen set of old models, sizes that do not match the published blobs,
 rotating version strings, and phrase-bank replies.

The behaviour matches no published
 honeypot, tarpit or mock-server project, checked against GitHub, the web, and the
 honeypot literature. The closest, funnypot, echoes the model name rather
 than the prompt and runs on a single host.

The causes are all guesses and range widely.
 A honeypot, though the bait is worthless. Real servers that refuse outside probes, and
 we watched one genuine box do exactly that. A coordinated deployment. Or a badly
 misconfigured setup copied onto thousands of machines and forgotten. We cannot choose
 between them from here. Narrowing it would take infrastructure work: reverse DNS, ASN
 and subnet clustering, and whether one operator's fingerprints recur.
