title: Flash flooding causes major damage to the Grand Canyon's critical water pipeline
description: The sole pipeline that supplies water for millions of Grand Canyon visitors was badly damaged by weekend flash flooding, setting up a tricky repair scenario and upending a yearslong construction proje...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The sole pipeline that supplies water for millions of Grand Canyon visitors was badly damaged by weekend flash flooding, setting up a tricky repair scenario and upending a yearslong construction project to upgrade the line laid over terrain so rugged helicopters are often required to make basic fixes.

Park officials said roughly 40% of the pipeline was damaged or destroyed. The long-term implications of the damage to the park's infrastructure, visitors and year-round residents weren't immediately clear. The 12.5-mile (20-kilometer) long Transcanyon Waterline has endured dozens of breaks in recent years. A more than $200 million repair and replacement project was well underway when the floods hit.

Caused by heavy rain, the floods killed at least two people, left more than a dozen others missing or unaccounted for and required the evacuation of more than 60 people. Officials said significant water reductions are needed — short showers, turning off the tap while brushing teeth and flushing toilets selectively to to protect the limited stored water on the South Rim, where most visitors go.

The pipeline, which was finished in the 1970s, has broken more than 85 times since 2010. It moves water from one side of the canyon, down to its base, across a bridge and back up the other side of the rough landscape. Any effort to fix a break from rock falls or flash floods is time-consuming, precarious and costly, so addressing the latest damage will be complicated.

The pipeline upgrade project, which began in 2023, took more than a decade to design, consider and fund. It involves moving the point where water would flow into the pipeline, installing helicopter pads, building water treatment facilities and replacing several miles of pipeline.

Basic decisions were complicated. For example, the original pipe was aluminum, which is lighter and easier to move into the steep canyon but is susceptible to breaking. Engineers picked a flex-steel material to balance weight with durability.

Even routine pipeline breaks force water restrictions. In 2016, a hotel on the canyon's rim that offers luxury dining and boasts about its history hosting presidents was forced to reduce dishwashing and use paper plates and plastic utensils.

The park had water conservation measure in place even before the latest bout of flooding and damage.

The flooding has forced parts of the park to close and additional flooding was possible Monday, according to the National Park Service.

"Consider changing your plans if you were going to hike, boat, or paddleboard to a slot canyon or normally dry wash. If you do still decide to recreate, check in at a nearby visitor center or ranger station," a notice on the park website said.

Officials said previously that the repair and replacement project would ensure that the park will be able to meet its water supply needs for the next 50 years or more. The park had roughly 4.4 million visitors last year.

When the original pipeline was nearing completion in the 1960s, more than a foot (0.3 meters) of rain fell, flooding the inner canyon. That rare historic flood caused 40% of the project to be destroyed, officials said.

title: Swansea sign Huddersfield midfielder Iorpenda
description: Swansea City complete permanent move for promising midfielder Tom Iorpenda from Huddersfield Town.
fullText:
Swansea City have completed the permanent signing of Huddersfield Town midfielder Tom Iorpenda.

The 21-year-old has joined the Championship club from the League One Terriers for an undisclosed fee, thought to be worth about £1m.

Iorpenda, whose Huddersfield deal was expiring next summer, has signed a three-year contract with the option of another 12 months.

Head coach Vitor Matos said: "Tom is a promising young player who has qualities that give us something different in midfield.

"He is an aggressive player who is confident in driving forward with the ball at his feet, but he also works very hard defensively, while having the quality to pick out progressive passes."

Swansea agree loan of Manchester City's Monga

Swansea can still improve after unbeaten start - Matos

The midfielder is in contention for a swift debut when the unbeaten Swans host Watford in the Championship on Tuesday, 1 September (19:45 BST).

Iorpenda, who was on the books of Brighton as a youngster, spent 2025-26 on loan at Notts County and helped them to promotion from League Two via the play-offs.

He made 53 appearances and scored three goals, with his exploits leading to him being named as player of the season by his Magpies team-mates and supporters.

Iorpenda's contract was due to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season and that led to Huddersfield "reluctantly" accepting what they call a "substantial" fee.

Huddersfield head coach Martin Drury said: "I'm disappointed he has chosen to leave our club as I believe our environment would have been a perfect fit for him and his development as both a player and person.

"However, I admire his ambition and I wish him every success for his future."

Iorpenda boosts a rebuilt Swansea midfield after the summer departure of Ethan Galbraith to Championship rivals Stoke City.

Matos added to his options with the signing of Canada international Stephen Eustaquio, who made his debut off the bench in the 3-0 win at Derby after signing from Porto.

title: Elliott expected to join Valencia on loan
description: Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is expected to join Valencia on loan for the rest of the season.
fullText:
Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is expected to join Valencia on loan for the rest of the season.

The 23-year-old spent last season on loan at Aston Villa but made only one Premier League start for them.

Valencia, who finished ninth in La Liga last season and did not qualify for Europe, had been working to find a financially viable way of making the loan deal work.

Elliott is yet to undergo a medical at Valencia. La Liga's transfer window closes on Tuesday at 23:00 BST.

The Spanish club want Liverpool to cover half of the midfielder's wages. It remains unclear what the exact wage split will be.

Sources indicate there is no option or obligation for Valencia to buy Elliott in the terms of the loan deal.

Elliott featured regularly during Liverpool's pre-season under new head coach Andoni Iraola but has subsequently been left out of the club's first two Premier League squads.

The former England Under-21 international's contract with Liverpool runs until 2028.

Elliott joined Liverpool from Fulham aged 16 in 2019 and spent the 2020-21 season on loan at Blackburn Rovers in the Championship.

Meanwhile, Liverpool defensive midfielder Stefan Bajcetic has joined boyhood club Celta Vigo on a permanent deal.

title: Mother tells how daughter slipped from her grasp in north Cyprus ferry disaster
description: KYRENIA, Cyprus, Aug 31 (Reuters) - Ayten Bicer felt her 12-year-old daughter slip from her hands and disappear as a ferry capsized off northern Cyprus on Sunday, killing at least eight people. Her da...
fullText:
KYRENIA, Cyprus, Aug 31 (Reuters) - Ayten Bicer felt her 12-year-old daughter slip from her hands and disappear as a ferry capsized off northern Cyprus on Sunday, killing at least eight people.

Her daughter Miray, and 6-year-old son Mehmet Asaf, ‌were among 20 people still missing on Monday as search teams looked for survivors in waters more than 500 metres (1,640 feet) ‌deep.

"She was saying, 'Don't let go'. And I didn't let go of my daughter. I swear, I didn't let her go," Ayten Bicer sobbed.

A suitcase fell on top of her, forcing ​the girl from her grasp. The mother caught hold of the daughter's foot, but her shoes, coated in engine oil from the overturned vessel, slipped through her hands.

The double-hulled ferry with 267 aboard took in water and flipped over on Sunday just off the port city of Kyrenia, leaving survivors clinging to the overturned hull. They were rescued by passing vessels and the coastguard authorities.

However, 20 people were still unaccounted for, including the Bicer siblings, in Cyprus ‌for a holiday.

Separate accounts said the wide-bodied vessel jolted ⁠violently before slamming on to the sea surface with part of its bow bursting open on impact. Severe storms hit Cyprus on Saturday and the seas were still rough on Sunday, when the disaster occurred.

Debris remained scattered across ⁠the water on Monday, including a black wheelie suitcase bobbing on the surface and a sheet of steel that appeared to have broken away from the ferry.

Authorities revised their figure of missing persons upwards to 20 from 18, after police cross-checked passenger manifests with survivors, officials said.

Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan ​Erhurman told ​reporters that a ship would be arriving from Turkey on Tuesday to help ​with the search for those missing.

"Intervening at the seabed is ‌not possible with the resources we currently have, but from tomorrow that intervention will be possible," he said.

It was unclear if people remained trapped on the vessel, now lying on the seabed.

Footage posted on social media suggested that at the time the ship flipped, there were still people trapped in one of its compartments.

Outside the port in Kyrenia, some of those waiting sat and silently wept, while others scrolled mobile phones for updates.

Ayten Bicer's husband, Hayri, said everything happened suddenly.

"We couldn't intervene. We lost our children. We made a lot of effort but we couldn't save our children. ‌Two of my children are gone. One of my sons is alive. Two of ​my children are gone. Two of my three children are gone. We left them. We ​are leaving them on this island as we go," he ​said.

The ferry ran into trouble shortly after leaving Kyrenia for the Turkish port of Tasucu, in Mersin province, one ‌of several daily sea shuttle links with Turkey.

Nine people connected ​to the vessel's operations were detained for ​three days by a court on Monday to assist police inquiries.

The vessel had a valid seaworthiness certificate, authorities said.

Ayten Bicer sat on a deck chair outside the port in Kyrenia on Monday, waiting for updates. Her eyes were swollen shut from crying.

"It was slipping ​like oil, there was diesel, our feet were slippery. ‌It was slippery everywhere. It was like oil. She slipped out of my hand. Mehmet Asaf held on to his ​father here," Ayten Bicer said, showing the collar of her T-shirt. "Saying, 'Baba' (Dad)".

title: India's Modi tells Russia's Putin that the war in Ukraine must end for humanity's sake
description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday that the war in Ukraine needed to end for humanity's sake and that New Delhi would
fullText:
MOSCOW, Aug 31 (Reuters) - Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi told Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday that the war in Ukraine needed ‌to end for humanity's sake and that New Delhi would support ‌every peace effort to stop the fighting.

Modi, who made his comments at the start of ​talks with Putin in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek, called Putin "my friend" and hailed growing economic ties between the two countries which he said were guided by the need to put the interests of both nations above all else.

India, along with ‌China, is one of ⁠the biggest buyers of Russian oil, which has helped Moscow replenish its budget since it sent tens of thousands of ⁠troops into Ukraine in 2022 and was hit with sweeping Western sanctions.

"As you are aware, India supports all peace efforts in this regard, and we shall continue ​to do ​so in the future," Modi told ​Putin on the sidelines of the ‌Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit, according to a Kremlin transcript of their exchange.

"Every day that the war continues, humanity is, in effect, set back a step, whilst every step towards peace gives all of humanity real hope for peace. We need to move from endless war to an end to the ‌war, to a cessation of hostilities. And we ​will need to move precisely in this ​direction," said Modi who has ​said before that he wants a peace settlement for Ukraine.

The ‌Kremlin - which has repeatedly said that ​Russia is only ready ​to end the war on its own terms, which Ukraine has dismissed as an unacceptable demand to capitulate - said after the talks that ​Putin had briefed Modi ‌on how the special military operation, Russia's preferred description for its ​action in Ukraine, was progressing, the state TASS news agency reported.

(Reporting ​by Reuters; Editing by Andrew Osborn)

title: 31-year-old millionaire has zero sympathy for unemployed Gen Z’s ‘excuses’—he says ‘it is scarily easy’ to build a business and get rich right now
description: As AI kills entry-level jobs, multimillionaire Timothy Armoo has a blunt message for unemployed Gen Zers: Stop making excuses and start building.
fullText:
Timothy (or Tim) Armoo became a millionaire before turning 30. Now, as Gen Zers blame a brutal job market and AI for their struggles, the millionaire entrepreneur isn't having any of it: He says this is actually the easiest moment in history to get rich.

"It is scarily easy" to build wealth right now, Armoo told Fortune. "This is the greatest era of wealth creation ever. And it kind of pains me when a lot of young people are like, 'I'm bored.' How can you be bored? This is the greatest technology ever in history, and you're not obsessing over it."

How are Gen Zers leveraging technology for entrepreneurship?

Why does Armoo think AI makes wealth creation easier?

What is the Legon Fund and its purpose?

How did Timothy Armoo become millionaire before 30?

He added, "In 2026, if you're talking about the small things [that you can do to become successful], one of the most obvious things is to build relatively small projects with AI."

Armoo knows more than most what it's like to make it, despite the odds being stacked against you. Sent to live with his grandmother in Ghana as a baby, he described the start of his life as "uncertain and dangerous." When he finally moved back to London, home became a council estate in the middle of gang violence and knife crime.

Yet despite arriving in the U.K. with no money, no network, and years of instability behind him, Armoo started his first business—a tutoring service—at just 14, scaling it to 65 tutors within six weeks. By 17, he already had an acquisition under his belt: the sale of his publication, Entrepreneur Express, to Horizon Media. In 2017, while most of his university peers were out partying, he spent his second year founding Fanbytes, an influencer marketing agency that went on to land clients like the U.K. government, Deliveroo, and Samsung. Brainlabs acquired it in 2022 for an eight-figure sum, when Armoo was just 27.

It's no secret that Gen Z don't want nine-to-five jobs. Research, surveys, and snap polls have consistently revealed that the latest generation of workers want to be their own boss—and Armoo says AI has made that dream more achievable than ever. He's put real money behind the claim, too.

"AI enables you to think of an idea and put it out into the world," Armoo added. "And social media means that you don't need to pay someone in order to do it. You just need to spend time on the platform and just keep posting."

And he's backing that up with cash. Armoo's just launched Legon Fund, where he's committed £5 million (around $6.7 million) of his own cash to fund AI startups founded by minority entrepreneurs.

"The reason I did that was that my wealth wave was social media," he explained. "Now I think the wealth wave is AI, and I don't want anyone to say, 'Well, I had the idea, but I didn't have the money to distribute it.'

title: El-Sayed tries to make peace with Jewish Democrats but draws line at dumping Hasan Piker
description: Abdul El-Sayed met with Michigan's Democratic Jewish Caucus to apologize, but Mike Rogers calls his remarks a "sham apology" amid antisemitism concerns.
fullText:
Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed spent this past weekend trying to mend fences with Jewish Democrats in Michigan, but his Republican rival calls El-Sayed's comments a "sham apology."

El-Sayed, in an appearance Saturday before the Michigan Democrats' Jewish Caucus, and in an answer to a question from Fox News Digital, apologized for comments he made after a March attack on a suburban Detroit synagogue. But he pushed back when asked to repudiate controversial comments from incendiary left-wing streamer Hasan Piker, who is a strong supporter of his campaign.

A vocal critic of Israel who describes its military actions against Hamas in Gaza as "genocide," El-Sayed is facing off against former Rep. Mike Rogers, the Republican nominee in the Great Lakes battleground state, for a crucial open Senate seat the Democrats must hold in the midterm elections as they aim to win back control of the chamber.

El-Sayed's narrow primary victory over more moderate Rep. Haley Stevens in what was a divisive intraparty showdown was arguably the biggest victory to date for the left in its battle against the establishment for the ideological future of the Democratic Party. El-Sayed appeared this past weekend at the state party's nominating convention in Lansing, Michigan in an effort to unify Democrats in the wake of the primary battle.

Democratic Michigan Ag Accuses Her Party Of 'Absolutely Not' Doing Enough To Counter Antisemitism

Fox News Digital asked El-Sayed about a recent controversy stemming from comments he made in response to an attack on a Michigan synagogue, when federal investigators say a gunman inspired and radicalized by Hezbollah crashed into the place of worship seeking to kill as many Jewish people as he could. The alleged attacker was a Lebanese-born man who a week earlier had lost relatives in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon.

"Hurt people, hurt people," El-Sayed said in response to the attack. He was criticized by members of his own party, including Michigan Secretary of State Dana Nessel, who discussed the comments in a recent interview with The Atlantic, and declined to attend this past weekend's convention partly over concerns of antisemitism in the Democratic Party.

El-Sayed told Fox News Digital his comments "might have been misconstrued to be justifying something I did not intend to justify," but then offered an apology.

"To anybody who feels like my comments may have been hurtful, I'm really sorry. That was not my intention. We condemned that terrorist attack. We condemned it outright," El-Sayed added. "What I was trying to do was offer context for why it happened, but it wasn't the time for context and you don't ever want to trample somebody's pain."

El-Sayed is an epidemiologist and former Wayne County Health Department director who, if elected in November, would make history as the nation's first Muslim senator. He has argued against unconditional U.S. military aid to Israel, as have other progressive politicians. And El-Sayed has repeatedly declined to directly answer whether Israel has the right to exist.

He said his message to Jewish voters in Michigan is, "We may not agree on everything when it comes to foreign policy... I'm not going to stop fighting for Palestinian self-determination... but that does not mean that I will not stand up… for safety for all communities and I believe in the safety and dignity of Jewish kids like I believe in the safety and dignity of my own kids."

Before taking questions from reporters, El-Sayed met in Lansing with the state's Democratic Jewish Caucus.

"He just had a very good meeting with us," Daniel Rivkin, a convention delegate and member of the caucus, told Fox News Digital, as he referred to El-Sayed. "We're having real conversations."

Check Out The Latest Fox News Poll In Michigan's Blockbuster Senate Race

The El-Sayee campaign is also in the process of hiring a Jewish liaison, Fox News Digital confirmed on Monday.

But some Jewish leaders in Michigan went public on Saturday with an open letter urging Jewish Democrats and independents in the state to sign their names in support of Rogers, who is making a second straight run for the Senate after falling just 20,000 votes short in 2024.

"Many of us have been fiercely supportive of Democratic candidates and principles. All of us have felt threatened and alienated by the politics and allies embraced by Abdul El-Sayed, which has included demonization of Jews, equivocation on terrorism, exclusion of Jewish Americans from public life, and expression of implacable hatred of the world's only Jewish nation," the letter stated.

Rogers, in a statement highlighting the letter, claimed that "Abdul El-Sayed fans the flames of antisemitism. We're fighting to extinguish it."

In an interview Monday morning on Fox News' "Fox and Friends," Rogers said, "We've had so many Democrat Jewish people here in the state of Michigan ring up our phone and say, "I can't do this. I'm for you."

What The Latest Fox News Power Rankings In The Midterm Races Show

Referring to El-Sayed, Rogers said, "When someone says you might have been offended by what I said, that's not an apology."

And he claimed that El-Sayed "has a long history of antisemitic and inflammatory comments."

But El-Sayed has repeatedly pushed back, saying, "My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own kids. We have a responsibility to take on antisemitism in all of its forms, wherever we see it."

Making El-Sayed's mission to make peace with Jewish Democrats and independents more difficult is the backing he receives from Piker.

Piker recently featured on his stream an image of state Sen. Jeremy Moss, the Democratic nominee in Michigan's 11th Congressional District. Moss, who is Jewish, has said that people are sharing a fake audio clip of him claiming that his entire reason for running for Congress is to make sure that America continues to support Israel.

"If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker warned.

Democracy '26: Stay Up To Date With The Fox News Election Hub

Piker, who endorsed El-Sayed for the Democratic nomination and appeared at some of the candidate's campaign events including a primary night party in Detroit, has repeatedly stood by his numerous past comments critical of Israel over its ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza.

El-Sayed, who over the past week appeared to try and distance himself from Piker, responded to the firestorm by saying, "I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople."

On Saturday, El-Sayed was peppered with questions from reporters about Piker.

"We're in the state of Michigan. If you want to make this race about a streamer in California, I just think you're missing the boat," El-Sayed told reporters. "This is about affordability in Michigan. This is about seeing a doctor in Michigan. This is about Donald Trump's disastrous policies in Michigan. That's what I'm focused on right now."

As the questions about Piker continued, El-Sayed repeatedly characterized him as "a streamer from California" who is irrelevant to his race in Michigan. "This is not a serious conversation."

These 12 Midterm Races Will Decide Which Party Controls The Senate

Besides his numerous antisemitic comments, Piker is known for saying "America deserved 9/11," praising Mao Zedong and Communist China, and arguing that capitalists should be murdered in the streets.

The Democrats' discord over Israel comes as most GOP leaders continue to showcase their support for Israeli leaders. As the Republican Jewish Coalition's annual leadership summit got underway Sunday evening in Las Vegas, El-Sayed and the far-left drew boos from the audience of high-powered GOP activists and donors.

Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters, speaking Monday at the RJC gathering, said that "the same hatred that fueled" the Oct. 7, 2023 large-scale attack by Hamas on Israel that killed about 1,200 people and triggered the ongoing war "is growing right here in our backyard."

"It has found a home in the Democratic Party. This did not happen overnight. It happened step-by-step as radical extremists took over the party, and the Democratic leaders let them," Gruters argued.

Meanwhile, there's no letup in the battle between the left and the center for the future of the Democratic Party.

Rahm Emanuel, a former ambassador, congressman, Chicago mayor and former White House chief of staff to then-President Barack Obama, took aim at the socialist push taking aim at the party's establishment.

"The Democratic Party is not open to being taken over," Emanuel, who's seriously mulling a 2028 White House run, told Fox News' Shannon Bream on "Fox News Sunday."

"I don't consider the Democratic Socialists are part of the Democratic Party. About four weeks ago, they had a convention in Chicago. Separate party. They believe in defunding police, letting prisoners out of prison, opening borders, eliminating the Pentagon. If you're so confident people want that, I'll see you in November. Put it on the ballot. Let's go. Run as a separate party," Emanuel emphasized.

Democratic Party leaders, when asked about the party's current ideological warfare, often point to Democrats as a "big tent" party.

But veteran Democratic strategist Julian Epstein criticizes such responses and jabs at his party for failing to call out the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

"They've taken cover behind the empty 'Big Tent" lie as radical DSA members and allies, like Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed and Colorado's Melat Kiros, triumph in Democratic primaries," Epstein wrote in an opinion piece last week in the New York Post.

Epstein, who served as chief counsel for the Democratic minority on the House Judiciary Committee during the 1998 impeachment proceeds against then-President Bill Clinton and who later served on Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign, argued, "Moderates should unite and shed the Big Tent delusion — because they have nothing to lose but their chains."

With the House of Representatives back in session, a resolution "condemning socialism in all its forms" could see a vote later this week.

Rep. Jeff Crank, R-Colo., introduced a measure Thursday condemning socialism in all its forms, telling Fox News Digital he wanted to use the vote to force moderate House Democrats to take a more public stance against the DSA.

Fox News' James Cirrone contributed to this report

title: Ukraine says its strikes on oil refineries have forced Russia to start importing jet fuel for its warplanes
description: Ukraine has been conducting a long-range strike campaign, hitting Russia's oil and gas facilities to try to hurt its economy and war effort.
fullText:
Ukraine said that its strikes on Russian oil facilities have pushed Moscow to import jet fuel.

Russia has a "shortage of domestic resources" as it tries to increase attacks and fly civilian jets.

Ukraine is attacking oil and gas facilities across Russia to try to hamper its fighting ability.

Ukraine said over the weekend that its strikes on Russian oil facilities have reduced production so much that Russia is now having to import fuel for its warplanes.

On Saturday, Ukraine's GUR, the country's military intelligence agency, said that "systematic and precise strikes by Ukraine's Defense Forces against Russia's oil-refining network have led to a significant reduction in jet fuel production in the Russian Federation."

It said that Russia's increasing air attacks against Ukraine, "combined with the need to sustain civilian air transport, have resulted in a shortage of domestic resources."

"To meet the needs of military and civilian aviation, Russia, which for decades has positioned itself as an energy superpower, has officially introduced a temporary ban on the export of its own aviation fuel and is being forced to seek ways to import foreign Jet A-1 aviation fuel," the GUR said.

That fuel is compatible with a range of Russian military aircraft used to launch missiles and bombs, as well as jet-powered drones. The GUR added that Russia is now fueling its Il-76MD-90A military transport with fuel outside manufacturer recommendations.

The GUR said that Russia had purchased at least 70,000 tonnes of aviation fuel from South Korea and Egypt that was delivered on three shadow fleet tankers. The fleet is a network of vessels that Russia uses to circumvent Western sanctions through hidden ownership, among other methods.

The GUR Saturday said that Russian efforts to "circumvent sanctions will inevitably receive an appropriate response."

Ukraine is conducting a major long-range strike campaign targeting oil and gas facilities inside Russia in a bid to damage the country's economy, which depends heavily on the energy sector, and frustrate its ability to continue its invasion of Ukraine. The strikes have hit targets hundreds of miles into Russia.

Ukraine refers to these strikes against Russia's economy as "long-range sanctions." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy promised this month that "there will be more Ukrainian deep strikes, which should demonstrate to Russia and the Russians that peace is necessary."

Ukraine has significantly increased the pace of these strikes this year and claimed a host of wins against targets this month, including strikes on refineries, processing facilities, and terminals. The country has said that some sites have halted operations as a result.

Zelenskyy said in June that nearly 40% of Russia's primary oil refining capacity was offline as of the previous month. And he said this month that it remains a priority for Ukraine.

Russia's economy is heavily dependent on oil and gas. Western sanctions have affected the industry, but Russia also received a reprieve when the war in Iran limited other energy sources by closing the Strait of Hormuz, a route Russia does not rely on. Kyiv is trying to restore some of that pressure.

Ukraine has primarily used homemade cruise missiles and drones to hit targets inside Russia. Though Western partners provided long-range weapons, restrictions on their use inside Russia forced Ukraine's booming defense industry to develop domestic solutions.

Ukraine has unveiled new weaponry with longer ranges in recent months to deepen its campaign, including drones with ranges exceeding 1,800 miles.

Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's former defense minister, said this month that Ukraine could be capable of hitting Russian territory with domestically made ballistic missiles within the next three to six months. These weapons typically have longer ranges and move much faster than cruise missiles.

Ukraine is fighting against barrages of Russian strikes on its territory that are stretching its air defenses thin. A key target Kyiv seeks to pursue is the missile launchers inside Russia.

Russia has been intensifying its strikes on Ukraine. Zelenskyy said on Sunday that in the last week, Russia launched almost 2,000 attack drones, more than 1,600 glide bombs, and 31 missiles, including North Korean ballistic missiles, at Ukraine.

Ukraine's long-range strike campaign, which is focused solely on legitimate military targets rather than cities and civilian infrastructure like Russian strikes, has yet to push Moscow toward negotiations for ending hostilities, but Kyiv hopes that the fuel shortages will raise the cost of the war and constrain some attacks.

title: Forest forward Hutchinson joins AC Milan on loan
description: AC Milan complete the signing of Omari Hutchinson on loan from Nottingham Forest until the end of the season.
fullText:
AC Milan have signed Omari Hutchinson on loan from Nottingham Forest until the end of the season.

The seven-time European champions will have the option to make the forward's move to the San Siro permanent at the end of the campaign.

Hutchinson's temporary exit from Forest comes 12 months after completing a £37.5m transfer from Ipswich Town.

Last season at the City Ground, he made only 17 Premier League starts under four different managers.

Hutchinson came through the ranks at Chelsea before moving to Arsenal and signing his first professional contract in 2020.

He returned to Stamford Bridge in 2022 and made two appearances for the Blues before joining Ipswich in 2023.

After initially joining the Tractor Boys on loan in 2023, Hutchinson's move was made permanent 12 months later after he helped them win promotion to the Premier League.

Hutchinson, who was part of the England Under-21 side that won the European Championship in 2025, will wear the number 20 shirt for Milan this season.

title: Forest complete £22m Munoz signing from Palace
description: Nottingham Forest complete the £22m signing of Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest have completed the £22m signing of Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace.

The Colombia right-back reunites with Oliver Glasner at the City Ground having won the FA Cup and Conference League together with the Eagles.

He has signed a three-year deal after spending the last two and a half years at Selhurst Park, scoring 11 goals in 109 appearances.

Munoz follows the £50m record arrival of Liam Delap and could make his debut against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League on Saturday.

He said: "I'm really excited because I can see so much talent, Forest is a team with great players, great qualities and great skills on the pitch, I can't wait to get out there so I can help my new team-mates and I think that we're going to do great things.

"It is a club that's fought hard in recent years, it has competed hard, it got to the semi-finals of the Europa League and I think it has even greater objectives for the future, and really this is what I like about Forest, and that's why I decided to come here."

Munoz, who has 51 caps, also helped Palace win the Community Shield in 2025.

Forest's chief football officer George Syrianos added: "Daniel has performed strongly in the Premier League and in European competition, and we believe he has the mentality and ambition to make a significant contribution to the club."

Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool on Saturday, having lost their opening two games in the Premier League and Carabao Cup to Leeds United.

title: Scotland beat Dutch by nine wickets to level series
description: Scotland level their one-day international series with the Netherlands at 1-1 after a thumping nine-wicket victory in a rain-affected match in Stirling.
fullText:
Second one-day international, Stirling

Netherlands 129-9 (32 overs): De Leede 58; Maqsood 3-20, Carter 2-18

Scotland 130-1 (16.2 overs): S Bryce 70*, Carter 33*

Scotland levelled their one-day international series with the Netherlands at 1-1 after a thumping nine-wicket victory in a rain-affected match in Stirling.

Sarah Bryce, captaining the side in the absence of her sister Kathyrn, led the way with an unbeaten 70 as the hosts chased down their target of 130 in just over half of their allotted 32 overs, in a game which was originally scheduled for Sunday but fell foul of the weather.

The Dutch had enjoyed a 58-run win in Glasgow on Friday and this was another one-sided contest.

Darcy Carter made an early breakthrough, taking the wickets of Netherlands openers Phebe Molkenboer and Sanya Khurana, who had piled on more than 150 in last week's encounter.

Abtaha Maqsood also took two quick wickets to leave the visitors reeling on 39-4.

Maqsood struck again but Babette de Leede made 58 before being run out, while Caroline de Lange added 20 on the way to their total of 129-9.

Scotland lost Maryam Faisal after four balls but Carter (33 not out) and Bryce made sure of a comprehensive success.

Wicketkeeper Bryce, who took two catches, settled the match with her 11th four, while the Dutch bowlers sent down 17 wides in 16 overs.

While it may have been a bruising defeat, the visitors do have cause for celebration since the completed match was enough to regain their ODI ranking and avoid a significant drop in funding.

The teams will meet again on Tuesday at the same venue to decide the series.

title: Smyth returns to Saints practice squad
description: Charlie Smyth is staying with the New Orleans Saints after the County Down kicker signed to their practice squad.
fullText:
Charlie Smyth will stay with the New Orleans Saints after the County Down kicker signed to their practice squad.

On Sunday, it was confirmed the Mayobridge man had not made the cut for a place on the NFC South franchise's 53-man squad before the start of the NFL season, and he was placed on the waiver wire.

It gave other teams the option to offer the former Gaelic footballer a contract, but that did not come to pass before Monday's 17:00 BST deadline.

Instead, Smyth will return to the Saints practice squad where he spent his entire first season and began last term, before making his debut when elevated to the full squad for a Week 13 defeat by the Miami Dolphins following Blake Grupe's release.

Smyth was also elevated in the following two weeks and a game-winning field goal against the Carolina Panthers was enough for him to earn a three-year contract for Kellen Moore's team as he saw out the season as first choice.

Last season, he made 12 of 16 field goal attempts and was perfect from 13 extra-point tries, putting him in a strong position to earn the number one slot for this season.

However, the 25-year-old had a mixed pre-season, initially facing competition from Tanner Brown before the Saints then brought in former Las Vegas Raiders' two-time All-Pro kicker Daniel Carlson whose 53-yard field goal won their final pre-season game against the Dallas Cowboys on Friday.

With Carlson winning the race for the number one spot, Smyth and Brown were waived with neither picked up by another team on Monday before the Saints finalised their 16-player practice squad.

As Smyth retains his international player pathway [IPP] status, he can be added as a 17th member and the Saints have decided to take up that option, ensuring he will remain in New Orleans for a third season since graduating from the IPP.

title: Sunderland agree loan deal with Spurs for Danso
description: Sunderland are set to sign defender Kevin Danso from Tottenham on a season-long loan, with an option for a permanent move.
fullText:
Sunderland are set to complete a season-long loan deal for Tottenham defender Kevin Danso.

BBC Sport revealed on Friday that Spurs had rejected an initial loan proposal for Danso, 27, from the Black Cats.

But the clubs have since reopened talks and agreed a deal in which Danso will move to the Stadium of Light on loan, with an option for Sunderland to make the move permanent.

Tottenham's imminent signing of centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo, 28, from Chelsea has unlocked Danso's move to Sunderland.

Spurs were previously unwilling to let the Austria international leave without finding a replacement.

Danso joined Spurs on loan from Lens in January 2025 and the deal was made permanent for £20.9m later that year.

title: Hull agree £22m fee for Everton's Iroegbunam
description: Hull City agree a £22m deal to sign Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.
fullText:
Hull City have agreed a £22m package to sign Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

The 23-year-old is poised to leave Hill Dickinson Stadium for an initial £13m, although the fee could rise by a further £9m with add-ons.

Iroegbunam, who joined Everton from Aston Villa for £9m in 2024, has been given permission to complete a medical in East Yorkshire.

It is part of a busy end to the transfer window for both clubs involved, with Hull looking to sign multiple players before Tuesday night's deadline.

Iroegbunam would become Hull's 13th signing of the summer, with talks continuing over a loan move for Chelsea midfielder Dario Essugo.

Everton, meanwhile, have agreed the £65m sale of winger Iliman Ndiaye to Manchester City.

They are close to signing Monaco striker Folarin Balogun and are in talks over moves for Manchester City winger Jack Grealish and Fulham defender Kenny Tete.

Talks over a return for Richarlison from Tottenham have stalled and his arrival on Merseyside is now not expected to happen.

title: Everton forced to move EFL Cup tie at short notice
description: Everton are forced to move their Carabao Cup third-round match against Championship side Wolves - nine days before it was due to be played.
fullText:
Everton have been forced to move their Carabao Cup third-round match against Wolves - just nine days before it was due to be played.

The last-32 fixture was scheduled for Wednesday, 9 September but will now take place seven days later.

The 9 September date was initially agreed to avoid a clash with a Liverpool home tie in the same competition, as the Reds' cup fixture with Tottenham was scheduled for 16 September after being chosen for a Sky Sports broadcast slot.

Because Wolves have Championship games on 13 and 20 September, but Everton are in Premier League action on 12 and 19, the EFL decided to move the cup game between the teams to the week before, as the most convenient date.

However, when Uefa released its Champions League fixtures line-up on Saturday, it was confirmed that Liverpool will start their European campaign against Atletico Madrid at Anfield on 9 September, while their cup game with Spurs has been moved to 15 September.

Merseyside Police does not allow both Liverpool and Everton to play at home on the same night.

European football's governing body Uefa said it was "not possible to make changes" to the Champions League tie because "the potential conflict only became apparent after the publication of the fixture lists".

Liverpool to face Tottenham in EFL Cup third round

Although the EFL appealed to Uefa to change the Liverpool-Atletico game date, European fixtures take precedence and the request was rejected.

The move means Everton's game with Wolves will now be played on Wednesday, 16 September, with Liverpool's Carabao Cup tie against Spurs brought forward by a day to Tuesday, 15 September.

A further knock-on effect is that Wolves' Championship game against Portsmouth must now be played after the first international break, on 20 October, rather than in September.

The EFL has apologised for making the changes at short notice but says it has been left with "no option", adding that Uefa's "unwillingness to co-operate" is "frustrating".

Uefa's expansion of its club competitions at one point seemed as though it would spell the end of two-legged EFL Cup semi-finals.

That has not happened, but there has still been a notable impact. Because the Champions League and Europa League start on different nights in September, an EFL Cup pre-draw now has to take place to ensure the clubs involved are not drawn against each other.

Uefa said it "does its best to accommodate reasonable requests wherever possible".

However, it added: "In this case, no issue had been raised with Uefa during the scheduling process, and the potential conflict only became apparent after the publication of the fixture lists.

"At that stage, it was not possible to make changes, particularly given the significant number of supporters who may already have arranged international travel and accommodation."

title: Touchline ban reduced for Rangers manager McInnes
description: Rangers manager Derek McInnes has a touchline ban reduced to two games, with two suspended, following an appeal against punishment for comments made on a last-gasp Celtic penalty.
fullText:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes has had a touchline ban reduced to two games, with two suspended, following an appeal against punishment for comments made on a last-gasp Celtic penalty during a television interview.

The 55-year-old will be in the stands for Wednesday's visit to Falkirk and Saturday's home match against Motherwell.

He will return to the dugout for the rescheduled visit of St Mirren to Ibrox on 9 September.

The original penalty of a four-match touchline ban, with one suspended, was issued in July and related to McInnes' spell as Hearts boss last season, when he described the decision to award Celtic a late penalty at Motherwell in May as "disgusting", adding "we are up against everybody".

The stoppage-time spot-kick for handball was converted by Kelechi Iheanacho and Celtic's 3-2 victory at Fir Park on 13 May kept them one point behind Hearts, who they beat to the title three days later in a final-day decider.

Rangers argued the remarks were "directed at the decision, rather than representing any broader criticism of officials" when announcing their intention to contest the ban.

At the same time, McInnes, said: "I've never wanted to make it personal. For me, the decision was wrong.

"Broadcasters pay a lot of money to hear managers' reactions. We've got to be careful that we don't have managers and players who have to be really sure of themselves and check themselves before answering a question.

"At no point was I wanting to inflame a situation. The situation was already being discussed before I did my press. It was quite a big moment in the season and there was a lot of emotion, but I felt as though what I said was controlled."

Rangers target Kelsy's colourful career - aged just 22

Is 'bitty' Pittodrie win turning point for McInnes and Rangers?

Visit our Rangers page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Speaking to Sky Sports after a win against Falkirk at Tynecastle on the same night as Celtic's win at Fir Park, McInnes said: "When you heard Celtic got a 96th-minute penalty that was going to VAR and they were checking it, you just assume what's happened is they get the penalty.

"Having seen it again, it's disgusting. It is. I don't think it's a penalty kick.

"But we're up against it. We're up against everybody."

Scottish FA head of referees Willie Collum later backed the call, citing "clear evidence" of Motherwell's Sam Nicholson's hand and arm "in an unnatural position" - and the resulting contact "a punishable handball".

The July statement from Rangers added: "Respect for officials and legitimate scrutiny are not competing principles.

"Managers, players and clubs must be able to speak honestly about major decisions if Scottish football is serious about raising standards and maintaining trust.

"Scrutiny, transparency and accountability should be seen as part of improving standards, not as a threat to them."

title: Far-left streamer Hasan Piker equates Israel's 'right to exist' to Nazi Germany
description: Hasan Piker compared Israel's right to exist to Nazi Germany and called Zionism a fascist ideology during his appearance on "The Breakfast Club."
fullText:
Far-left streamer Hasan Piker equated Israel's "right to exist" to Nazi Germany on Saturday during an interview on "The Breakfast Club," calling it an "apartheid state."

"I think Israel in its current formation, given that it's a settler colonial operation that's seeking out the expulsion or complete extermination of the indigenous population as an apartheid state does not have a right to exist," he said. "It's like, for me, it's like saying does Nazi Germany have a right to exist or does apartheid South Africa have a right to exist? Does Rhodesia have a right to exist? No, of course not."

Host of "The Breakfast Club," Charlamagne tha God, asked if it was like saying MAGA didn't have a right to exist, and Piker said yes.

"That doesn't mean kill all Republicans or whatever, right? I mean, I'm sure that's how people would present it as. I mean, this is a trick that every political movement deploys, right?" Piker responded.

Hasan Piker Claims Israel Has No 'Right To Exist' In Its Current Form

Who Is Hasan Piker? Meet The Far-left Streamer Who Is Stirring Up Controversy And Dividing Democrats

He added, "So the, 'Does Israel have a right to exist?' deployment as a statement, as a question, is a technique to shift the conversation away from Israel's crimes against the Palestinians to make it seem like the opposition is actually being crazy, and they want like all Jews to be exterminated, all Israelis to be exterminated, which is not the case. That's not a real point of advocacy, it's certainly not my advocacy," the streamer continued.

UCLA professor Benjamin Radd refuted Piker's characterization of Israel in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"Piker's comments about Israel as a 'settler colonial operation' and its alleged objective of 'seeking out the expulsion or complete extermination' of one of the region's indigenous groups reflects a profound ignorance of the historical development of the land, and of the various ethnic, religious, and colonial-imperial powers — including the Ottoman Turks — that have traded control over it. If Piker were intellectually honest, he could hold two uncomfortable truths simultaneously: that different groups, including Jews, have legitimate indigenous claims and that the current Israeli leadership does not represent nor serve as an indictment of those claims," Radd said.

Piker, an outspoken anti-Israel voice, also compared Zionism to fascism and Nazi Germany during the conversation.

"I think the reason why the Israeli society broadly has shifted so far to the right in a matter of decades is because of this ideology that guides Israeli society. It's Zionism, which I, by the way, have no problems like, equating to fascism because it is a fascist ideology and even make these comparisons to Nazi Germany, which is very frustrating for a lot of people. They say that's antisemitic," he said.

Piker has divided the Democratic Party, as some have chosen to embrace the streamer and others have denounced him.

Hasan Piker Calls Hamas 'Far More Moderate,' Dismisses Terror Group's Brutal Rule In Gaza

Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has campaigned with Piker and has dismissed any focus on his controversial statements. Though, recently, El-Sayed has put some distance between himself and the streamer.

El-Sayed, who is facing off against former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in battleground Michigan in a high-stakes Senate showdown, on Monday emphasized in a statement, "I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople."

The statement from El-Sayed came after Piker, on his stream last week, featured an image of state Sen. Jeremy Moss, the Democratic nominee in Michigan's 11th Congressional District. Moss, who is Jewish, has said that people are sharing a fake audio clip of him claiming that his entire reason for running for Congress is to make sure that America continues to support Israel.

Democrat Rips Hasan Piker As 'Hack Who Thrives On Hate' Over His Warning To American Jews About Israel

"If Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone is going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker warned.

Piker, who endorsed El-Sayed for the Democratic nomination and appeared at some of the candidate's campaign events, including a primary night party in Detroit, has repeatedly stood by his numerous past comments critical of Israel over its ongoing war against Hamas in Gaza.

Fox News Digital reached out to The Anti-Defamation League and The Jewish Federation for comment.

title: Newsom hit with lawsuit threat as whistleblower begs Trump for help with ‘monumental’ fraud scandal
description: Assemblyman Carl DeMaio says he plans to file a lawsuit against Gavin Newsom's new California law that he claims criminalizes citizen journalism.
fullText:
California's "monumental problem" with rampant fraud is about to get significantly worse, according to Republican state Assemblyman Carl DeMaio, after Gov. Gavin Newsom signed a bill that he warns will crack down on people investigating scammers.

Officially titled "Privacy for immigration support services providers," the new law creates privacy protections for immigration support service providers, employees and volunteers, including shielding their addresses and imposing penalties on those who publish their images on social media. DeMaio told Fox News Digital the bill amounts to criminalizing investigative journalism and works to "silence citizen journalists and shield taxpayer-funded organizations from public scrutiny."

"What does the Stop Nick Shirley Act do? It basically makes it illegal for a citizen journalist to document fraud of taxpayer money and post that on the internet in the form of an internet video," he said.

Newsom signed the bill into law last week, and it is set to take effect Oct. 1, 2027. DeMaio told Fox News Digital that he and a "coalition of civil liberty protectors" are prepared to file a lawsuit challenging the law.

Dems Ripped For 'Stop Nick Shirley Act' That Could 'Shield' Fraud And Abuse In California

"We have a plaintiff and are putting together the legal briefs," he said, adding, "It is a matter of time before we're going to get before a judge to stop this act."

"It is our hope," he continued, "that the U.S. Department of Justice will file to intervene in that case, because this is an open-and-shut infringement on our First Amendment rights."

DeMaio said California's fraud scandal makes the Minnesota fraud look like "garden variety government mismanagement."

"If you were worried about Somali daycare centers in Minnesota not having children in the daycare, take a look at California government NGOs receiving taxpayer funds and not having any sort of public services that they're delivering," he said. "They say they provide public services to immigrants when, in fact, they organize rallies, they harvest ballots, they endorse candidates and ballot measures during campaigns, and they are an extension of the Democrat Party."

DeMaio said the planned lawsuit follows discussions with the Justice Department's Office for Civil Rights.

Nick Shirley Warns California Bill Could Punish People Trying To Expose Government Fraud

"I have asked the U.S. Department of Justice Office of Civil Rights to look at the Stop Nick Shirley Act … to see if they can do anything to intervene to prevent the implementation of this law. We have been dialoguing with the Department of Justice, and now we have a game plan as to how we will proceed forward in the courts to overturn this unconstitutional law," he said.

Addressing Newsom directly, DeMaio said, "Gavin Newsom, once again, you're a bully trying to silence citizen watchdogs into not exercising their First Amendment rights and exposing your fraud, the billions of dollars that you've allowed to be wasted of precious taxpayer funds, all because you want the benefit of these left-wing NGOs to help you politically."

DeMaio said Newsom and California's Democratic supermajority "created such a monumental problem with fraud of taxpayer money being abused that it's clear that it is intentional."

"You're going to be exposed as a bully," he told Newsom. "You're going to be exposed as the fraud ringleader."

In response, Newsom spokesperson Diana Crofts-Pelayo told Fox News Digital that "this law has nothing to do with Nick Shirley" and that "the real controversy here is that MAGA Republicans are either lying to create up fake conspiracy theories, or none of them know how to read."

Crofts-Pelayo said the law does not affect Shirley's journalism, which Newsom's office previously referred to as "grifting" and "lying," and does not hide fraud.

title: 'It's an unknown' - Capsey takes England gloves for first time
description: Alice Capsey will keep wicket for England this week despite having only done it once in her career, but remains confident of successfully doing the job.
fullText:
When England gathered for their pre-series photo shoot on Monday, Alice Capsey had to remember an extra piece of kit.

Capsey has batted and bowled for her country. She has also grown to be one of their most reliable fielders and is talked of as a future leader aged 22.

But she also needed her wicketkeeping gloves because in this week's one-day international series against Ireland, she will be England's keeper, despite having only done the job once in a professional match - a 50-over game for South East Stars in 2020.

"Realistically, it is a bit of an unknown," Capsey tells BBC Sport. "In games, I have not done it a huge amount.

"But the work I have done off the pitch, I know I am putting a lot of hard work in. It gives me a lot of confidence."

In truth, this is not a punt in the dark. Coach Charlotte Edwards is not fond of those.

England first discussed having Capsey, who was a wicketkeeper for much of her junior career, as an option during their pre-season camp in South Africa earlier this year.

Amid a dearth of alternatives and after some early-season work, the 22-year-old was listed as the back-up to regular keeper Amy Jones for this summer's T20 World Cup.

She was never needed but when captain Nat Sciver-Brunt returned from injury for England's semi-final, the idea of in-form batter Sophia Dunkley keeping her place, Jones missing out and Capsey taking the gloves was on the table before ultimately being dismissed.

"Especially at the beginning of the summer, I was pretty nervous to do it," Capsey says.

"I went into my shell a little bit and was quite internal. It was awesome to have Sophie Ecclestone and those characters who are outgoing, jokey and keep everything relaxed.

"Everyone has seen me train so much now over the course of the summer it is second nature."

Like all good keepers, Capsey loves the rough and tumble that comes with the job.

"The amount of times you take blows on the fingers, or one goes down the leg side and you miss it..." she says.

"But those are the bits you enjoy, working to get better and better."

Capsey was a keeper when she came through the Surrey academy, only putting down her gloves when she started playing for a higher age group short of an off-spinner.

"Who knows if I hadn't played up whether I would have just kept on keeping, but it is really cool going back to the roots and where I started," she says.

England 'just humans' as Ireland target ODI upset

Dean to captain England against Ireland

Her time at Bede's School in Sussex also coincided with that of former England wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor, who worked there as a sports coach before moving back into the professional game where she now works with England's men.

It gave Capsey - a 12-year-old spectator in the stands when Taylor and England won the 2017 World Cup at Lord's - the chance to work with her wicketkeeping hero who is regarded as one of the best keepers the world has seen.

"The way she went about it, did it her way and brought an X-factor to it was really cool," Capsey says.

"She has been on my shoulder for the last four or five years saying I need to get back to keeping.

"It has been awesome to touch base with her, especially this summer to be able to message her and say 'I am back'."

Capsey began ramping up her glovework in training at the start of the summer, fitting drills around her batting, bowling and out-fielding.

She has also had to tweak her sessions in the gym to strengthen her legs and, in particular, her abductors for those squats behind the stumps.

"I have pulled up, touch wood, after all of it so far," Capsey says. "Come back to me at the end of the week."

And while it is six years since her last official outing, Capsey did keep behind closed doors in one of England's warm-ups against India before the T20 World Cup.

She took a tidy, rising catch off seamer Dani Gibson while standing up to the stumps, a stumping off spinner Linsey Smith and did not concede a bye.

"It was awesome," Capsey says. "I loved the experience.

"Keeping up to Gibbo was a really nice challenge.

"That catch was one of the highlights but also it is the little things, whether in the first over stood back to [Lauren] Filer and getting one cleanly in the hands, there were a couple of leg-side takes as well."

Capsey has also been standing up to the stumps to Issy Wong, one of England's quicker bowlers, in training this week.

The wider knock-on could be intriguing, if these three one-day internationals go well.

At the very least, it will provide a convenient back-up to 33-year-old Jones, who has been rested for this series, and some competition for places.

And, after Jones returned five single-figure scores in seven World Cup innings this year, it could free up a space for a more explosive batter in England's top order, given Capsey has already cemented her place in the team through her batting alone.

"There is going to be nerves and pressure around, but more internal pressure than anything," Capsey says.

"As a professional athlete you don't want to do it badly and you are representing England.

"It is an international series, there are ICC points on the line.

"To be trusted to have the gloves for England has got to give you confidence as well.

"I am not the finished article by any means but I did it for a long time growing up.

"Regardless of the challenges presented this week I know I have a bit of experience to fall back on which is nice."

title: Sabalenka blocks out noise to start US Open 'three-peat' bid with victory
description: Aryna Sabalenka blocks out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka blocked out the noise to overcome a tricky first-round test against Camila Osorio and begin her bid for a historic US Open "three-peat".

The two-time defending champion has suffered a dip in form in recent months after a stellar start to the season in which she reached the Australian Open final and completed the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami.

Sabalenka's position as world number one is now under serious threat and she risks ending the year without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022.

However, she avoided an early slip-up as she held off a resilient Osorio to win 6-2 6-4 on her return to Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"I really feel my best emotions at this stadium so it means a lot to be back and have an opportunity for a 'three-peat'," Sabalenka said.

"I'm trying to focus on myself. I'm enjoying my time in New York and I'm ready to go out here and do anything it takes to get the wins.

When Sabalenka lifted the Miami Open trophy in April, she established a 3,000-point lead at the top of the world rankings.

But early exits - by her high standards at least - followed at the French Open and Wimbledon. Now, Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina, who faces American wildcard Thea Frodin on Tuesday, trails her by just 434 points.

It means that Sabalenka, who is defending 2,000 points at Flushing Meadows, will have to win the title and hope Rybakina falls before the semi-finals to extend her 99-week reign as world number one.

Home favourites Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff could also secure the number one ranking with a title triumph.

Should Sabalenka win a third successive US Open title, she would become only the third woman to do so in the Open era after Serena Williams and Chris Evert.

However, she will need to improve considerably to navigate a stacked draw in New York.

Sabalenka stormed through the first set against the 52nd-ranked Osorio but struggled in the second, landing 48% of her first serves and hitting 12 unforced errors.

But the four-time major singles champion fended off three break points and struck decisively at 4-4 before serving out victory after one hour and 28 minutes.

Sabalenka will face Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko next.

title: Trump ally Laura Loomer faces criticism over racist comments against Black women
description: Multiple lawmakers and rights advocates condemned U.S.
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Aug 31 (Reuters) - Multiple lawmakers and rights advocates condemned U.S. President Donald Trump's ally Laura Loomer on Monday ‌over her racist comments attacking Democratic socialist Florida State Representative Angie ‌Nixon, as well as other prominent Black U.S. politicians and a Supreme Court justice.

"Angie Nixon ​is a ghetto, black, communist," Loomer, a right-wing blogger, conspiracy theorist and Trump ally, said on X on Monday, while doubling down after previous similar comments from her sparked widespread criticism.

On Friday, she cast Nixon, U.S. Representatives ‌Ilhan Omar and Ayanna Pressley, ⁠former U.S. Representative Cori Bush and U.S. Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson - all of whom are Black women - ⁠as "ghetto, entitled, race-obsessed, destructive black BITCHES who are completely unfit for the power they hold."

Nixon recently scored an upset victory in Florida's Democratic primary race for ​the ​U.S. Senate.

Loomer has also often made anti-Muslim ​comments, ranging from calling for ‌Muslims to be banned from holding office in the U.S. to advocating for deporting and removing "all Muslims from America."

"You attack and insult Black women because you believe peddling racism is good for your clicks and your business model," Maryland Governor Wes Moore said in response to Loomer.

U.S. Representative Rashida ‌Tlaib, a Palestinian American who herself has ​been attacked by Loomer, said "anti-Black racism goes ​unchecked."

U.S. House of Representatives Minority ​Leader Hakeem Jeffries called Loomer a "stone-cold racist."

Loomer has long ‌been one of the Republican president's ​most fervent supporters and ​is known to have Trump's ear.

"Black women should NEVER have to endure such hateful and degrading rhetoric for daring to lead," prominent ​civil rights attorney Ben ‌Crump said on Monday.

The Council on American Islamic Relations said ​Loomer's comments "are the very definition of anti-Black racism."

title: Mudryk to Spurs as Chelsea's Sanchez heads to Como
description: Chelsea accept offers from Tottenham for winger Mykhailo Mudryk and defender Tosin Adarabioyo, as well as a bid from Italian club Como for goalkeeper Robert Sanchez.
fullText:
Chelsea have accepted offers from Tottenham for winger Mykhailo Mudryk and defender Tosin Adarabioyo, as well as a bid from Italian club Como for goalkeeper Robert Sanchez.

The trio are now expected to leave Stamford Bridge, subject to agreeing personal terms, with Spurs keen to secure Mudryk, 25, and reunite him with his former manager Roberto de Zerbi.

The Ukraine international has not played a competitive match since November 2024, serving a suspension that followed an adverse finding for the banned substance meldonium, but he has been eligible to football since July.

Mudryk previously played under De Zerbi at Ukrainian side Shakhtar Donetsk before moving to Chelsea for an initial £61m.

Spurs will also sign Chelsea defender Adarabioyo, 28, on a permanent deal to replace Kevin Danso, who is set to join Sunderland on an initial loan.

In addition, Como, who signed defender Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea for £31m earlier in the transfer window, have agreed a season-long loan move for Sanchez.

Sanchez, 28, was made available for loan or permanent transfer after two mistakes in Chelsea's opening Premier League match at Fulham led to the Blues conceding twice.

Chelsea have since signed a replacement, bringing in Argentine Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa for £7.5m.

There remains uncertainty over the future of Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, who is attracting interest from Manchester City, although no formal offer has been made.

Any departure for Fernandez would be dependent on Chelsea strengthening their squad and receiving a substantial fee, having previously valued him at £120m.

title: Everton agree £40m fee for Monaco striker Balogun
description: Everton agree a £40m deal with Monaco for United States striker Folarin Balogun.
fullText:
Everton have agreed a £40m deal for Monaco forward Folarin Balogun.

The Toffees want to strengthen their forward line before Tuesday's transfer deadline, with Balogun, 25, and Tottenham's Richarlison among their targets.

Brazil forward Richarlison, 29, is believed to have reservations about returning to Everton, the club he left to join Spurs in 2022.

But Everton have pressed ahead with their interest in United States striker Balogun, who left boyhood club Arsenal to join French side Monaco in 2023.

Balogun has scored 31 goals in 91 matches across all competitions for the Ligue 1 team, while he has 12 goals from 31 caps for the USA.

Tottenham had agreed with Everton on Friday evening for Senegal winger Iliman Ndiaye, 26, to join the London club, with Richarlison moving the other way in a separate transfer.

However, sources are indicating Richarlison failed to agree personal terms with former club Everton, who are understood to have made a £35m offer for him.

Manchester City have subsequently agreed a deal worth up to £65m for Ndiaye.

Balogun was at the centre of a major controversy during this summer's World Cup, after he was dismissed for serious foul play against Bosnia-Herzegovina in the last 32 match and should have received an automatic suspension.

However, Fifa's disciplinary committee suspended his ban for a year - a decision that prompted widespread condemnation, particularly when it emerged US President Donald Trump and White House officials had lobbied football's world governing body about the American's sanction., external

Balogun, who scored three goals at the World Cup, was able to start the USA's last-16 defeat by Belgium - a decision European football's governing body Uefa called "unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable".

The head of Fifa's disciplinary committee refused to answer BBC questions about the decision-making process which led to Balogun avoiding a ban.

Meanwhile, Fifa president Gianni Infantino denied having influence over disciplinary decisions.

title: Kushner states regret over World Cup sell-off plan
description: Venture capitalist Joshua Kushner says he would not have got involved in Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup if he had known how the football world reacted.
fullText:
Venture capitalist Joshua Kushner, who was set to be the lead investor in Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup, says he now regrets joining the proposal.

In his first public comments since the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme sparked a major crisis for the governing body, Kushner said: "Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved".

The brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Kushner added he had "failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football".

However, he also defended the proposal, saying, "we stand behind the motivations of FFE", and that its intention "was to direct more capital and equity equally" among Fifa's 211 member associations.

Thrive Eternal, a firm founded by Kushner, had held talks with Infantino about heading up a $4.2bn (£3.1bn) investment in 20% of a new Fifa commercial subsidiary, before the idea was abandoned days after it was revealed in July amid a huge backlash.

Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?

Is football AI-proof? Why tech investors wanted a slice of the World Cup

Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino

Kushner's comments come just days after Uefa asked a court in New York to approve subpoenas for testimony and documents from both the American billionaire and Thrive as it considers lodging a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland.

European football's governing body Uefa has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down.

In a statement, Kushner said: "Money in football has historically been concentrated amongst a small group of countries.

"The idea behind FFE was to direct more capital and equity equally amongst all 211 member countries, providing significantly more investment to underdeveloped nations to nurture local talent, support grassroots football, enhance the fan experience, and ultimately grow the global game everywhere.

"It was an idea that every member association would vote on, not an obligation or determination.

"While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to. Thrive has a long track record of being a partner to all constituents. Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

In late July, shortly before scrapping the plan, Fifa said, "Thrive Eternal...is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE", claiming it would have seen the funding distributed to each national association for the 2027-2030 cycle increase from £5.9m to £14.7m.

As well as Kushner, Uefa has asked for the disclosure of documents from two Fifa businesses in the US and American financier Greg Maffei, who was a key adviser on the deal.

While Uefa says neither Kushner nor Maffei are anticipated defendants in any legal proceedings, it claims the pair first discussed the FFE concept in July 2025 and that Infantino had "been discussing the underlying concept with Kushner for nearly a year before the terms sheet was ultimately signed."

Its lawyers also argue the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at around £15bn, which it says is "a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". It claims Infantino failed to consult Fifa's hierarchy over the plan.

Kushner has recently agreed a deal to buy basketball's Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5bn (£9.3bn).

title: California mom has both legs amputated after suspected impaired driver plows into her restaurant lunch table
description: A California woman underwent three surgeries and a bilateral leg amputation after an alleged impaired driver crashed into a Boyle Heights restaurant.
fullText:
An elderly California mother had both her legs amputated after an alleged impaired driver crashed into the outdoor dining area of a restaurant where she was eating lunch.

Cristina Vargas, 81, was enjoying lunch at a sidewalk table outside Los Cinco Puntos in Los Angeles' Boyle Heights with her daughter, Gabriela Vargas, and their male friend when the SUV plowed into them at around 3:30 p.m. on July 7.

Surveillance footage obtained by KTLA shows an SUV veering onto the sidewalk and into the outdoor dining area.

Screeching tires were heard just before the SUV hit the group, sending patrons, the table and other items flying.

Arizona Grandpa To Undrgo Amputation After Collapsing On Scorching Sidewalk

"I remember I just heard screeching, and I was lifting up my head and I just saw headlights and a bumper and I heard a big boom," Gabriela told KTLA. "The next thing I knew, I was airborne."

Cristina's lower body was pinned under the vehicle and Gabriela suffered a head injury and a deep laceration on her knee. The two women and their male friend were rushed to a hospital for treatment.

Gabriela and the male friend have since recovered from their injuries, but Cristina's injuries were significantly worse, and she faces a long road to recovery.

Cristina underwent three surgeries and later had both of her legs amputated. She said she is thankful to be alive and has maintained a positive mindset.

She has been undergoing physical therapy at a rehabilitation center and will soon be allowed to go back home.

Cristina, a widowed mother of two, said she is looking forward to being surrounded by her family and friends.

"My goal is to give her the best quality of care from here on out," Gabriela said of her mother.

A police report alleges that the driver was impaired at the time of the crash. The unidentified woman was arrested and charged with multiple felonies, according to KTLA.

A GoFundMe created by a friend for the Vargas family has raised more than $30,000 as of Sunday night. The fundraiser said the family is facing massive medical bills, ongoing rehabilitation and daily living expenses.

"Cristina will need significant support to adapt to her new disability, including making their home accessible and covering the costs of specialized care. The road ahead is long and challenging, but with your help, they can focus on healing rather than the overwhelming financial stress," the fundraiser reads.

California Man Picks Up Explosive Device On A Beach During July 4 Cleanup, Loses Hand

The fundraiser described Cristina as a "vibrant and social person with a true lust for life."

"She loved to dance and was a regular at events at the senior center, bringing joy and energy wherever she went," the GoFundMe reads. "Her vivacious spirit and love for connecting with others made her a beloved member of the community. This sudden change is especially heartbreaking for someone who has always embraced life so fully and actively."

In an Aug. 17 update, Gabriela thanked supporters and said the recovery was progressing slowly.

"Thank you everybody for your love and support. We greatly appreciate it. It's a slow recovery but day by day we're getting through it. My mom's spirits remain hopeful as do mine. Recovery is very painful but she's giving it her all," Gabriela said.

title: Apple may change 'Lake Ontario' to 'Lake America' soon after talk with Trump, U.S. Interior Secretary says
description: U.S.
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Aug 31 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump has spoken to Apple about changing ‌the name of "Lake Ontario" to "Lake America" and ‌the company may soon alter its maps, Interior Secretary Doug ​Burgum said on Monday.

Trump announced on Thursday that he was changing the name of the smallest of the five Great Lakes, part of an ‌escalating trade feud ⁠with Canada that has prompted the two countries to impose reciprocal tariffs ⁠on billions of dollars in goods.

"The president reached out to Apple directly, so I'm sure that ​we may ​be seeing that ​change coming up soon ‌to Lake America," Burgum said in an interview on Fox Business' "Mornings with Maria" program.

Apple could not be immediately reached for comment.

The president's executive order on the name change affects the U.S. ‌Geographic Names Information System (GNIS), which ​sets the standards for official ​U.S. maps. It ​does not have any impact ‌on Canadian naming conventions or ​how the ​rest of the world refers to the lake.
